This file walks through our experiment in the order we spent the pull budget. For each step we explain what we did and why, show the code we ran (with file names and line numbers from our repository), and then show the output. Steps 0 and 2 ran on our own computers and used no pulls; Steps 1, 3 and 4 used the live server.

The problem and our approach

A website can combine 4 call-to-action buttons with 6 media options, giving 24 arms numbered 0 to 23. Each pull shows one arm to 100 visitors and returns how many of them sign up. Our group had 1,000,000 pulls (100 million visitors) and our goal was to maximise total sign-ups, so every pull spent on a weaker arm cost us sign-ups. The budget, the server's pull counter and the limit of five requests per second are shared by the whole group, so we agreed that one person would run a single driver for every live pull.

Our approach in short: we compared methods on invented data before spending any pulls, took a small live pilot, chose the method and its setting by simulating the rest of the budget from the pilot, and then ran that method on the live server, stopping at fixed checkpoints to check the data before committing more of the budget. During the long final run, the driver rechecked its setting every 200,000 pulls.

To make sure no pull was lost or counted twice, our driver saves every request (its arm, pull counter and request ID) to a local SQLite database before sending it. If a response is lost, the driver retries the same request with the same ID, following the handout's recovery steps, and it saves each response in the same transaction that clears the pending request. Step 0: screen methods on invented worldsOffline · 0 pulls

Before making any live pull, we built a simulator with invented conversion rates to see how different methods behave. It never contacts the server. We tested the three methods from our original plan (explore-first, ε-greedy and UCB1), adaptive ε-greedy from Lecture 9, and Thompson Sampling. We ran each setting 100 times in each of six kinds of world over the full 1,000,000 pulls, starting from 100 pulls per arm. Because the rates are invented, we used this step only to decide which methods to carry forward.

offline_simulation/simulate.py (beside the repo) · run_loop · lines 157–210one pull at a time for UCB, Thompson Sampling and ε-greedy
157def run_loop(cfg, P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, rng, horizon=T):
158    """One pull at a time, vectorised across replications."""
159    reps = len(P0)
160    idx = np.arange(reps)
161    kind = cfg['kind']
162    n, s = n0.copy(), s0.copy()
163    mu = s / (V * n)
164    P = P0
165    best = P.max(axis=1)
166    regret = V * ((best[:, None] - P) * n).sum(axis=1)
167    isq = 1 / np.sqrt(n)
168    sd = np.sqrt(mu * (1 - mu) / (V * n))
169    points = {int(t): i for i, t in enumerate(CURVE_POINTS)}
170    curve = np.full(len(CURVE_POINTS), np.nan)
171    t0 = int(n.sum(axis=1)[0])
172    c = cfg.get('c', 0.0)
173    eps = cfg.get('eps', 0.0)
174
175    for t in range(t0 + 1, horizon + 1):
176        if change_at == t:
177            P = P1
178            best = P.max(axis=1)
179
180        if kind == 'ucb':
181            arms = (mu + c * math.sqrt(2 * math.log(t)) * isq).argmax(axis=1)
182        elif kind == 'ts':
183            arms = (mu + sd * rng.standard_normal((reps, K))).argmax(axis=1)
184        elif kind == 'ts_exact':
185            arms = rng.beta(1 + s, 1 + V * n - s).argmax(axis=1)
186        else:
187            rate = eps if kind == 'eps' else min(1.0, c * K / t)
188            arms = mu.argmax(axis=1)
189            explore = rng.random(reps) < rate
190            count = explore.sum()
191            if count:
192                arms[explore] = rng.integers(0, K, count)
193
194        p = P[idx, arms]
195        rewards = draw(rng, p, batch_sd)
196        regret += V * (best - p)
197        new_n = n[idx, arms] + 1
198        new_s = s[idx, arms] + rewards
199        new_mu = new_s / (V * new_n)
200        n[idx, arms] = new_n
201        s[idx, arms] = new_s
202        mu[idx, arms] = new_mu
203        if kind == 'ucb':
204            isq[idx, arms] = 1 / np.sqrt(new_n)
205        elif kind == 'ts':
206            sd[idx, arms] = np.sqrt(new_mu * (1 - new_mu) / (V * new_n))
207        if t in points:
208            curve[points[t]] = regret.mean()
209
210    return finish(regret, mu, n, P if P1 is None else P1, rng, curve)

What we learned
  • Thompson Sampling and UCB with a scaled-down bonus (×0.02 to ×0.05) lost the fewest sign-ups in every fixed-rate world, about 7,000 to 20,000.
  • UCB1 with the lecture's bonus (×1) lost 0.9 to 1.2 million. Its bonus is sized for rewards as noisy as a single 0-or-1 outcome, but the conversion rate of a 100-visitor batch is far less noisy, so it kept exploring.
  • Explore-first and ε-greedy depended heavily on their setting, and explore-first could not recover from an early wrong pick.
  • When the rates changed part-way through, every method lost heavily, so we planned noise and stability checks at each live checkpoint.
  • A bigger pilot only cost sign-ups when the method kept learning afterwards, so we cut our live pilot from the planned 100 pulls per arm to 10.

Step 1: live pilotLive · 240 pulls

We pulled every arm 10 times in rotation: 240 pulls, or 0.024% of the budget. We made a single test pull first to confirm that live pulls worked and returned the expected fields, and made the other 239 once it checked out. Our uniform model always pulls the least-pulled arm (the lowest number on ties), so the pilot sampled every arm evenly over time. We chose 10 pulls per arm rather than the 100 in our original plan because Step 0 showed that a bigger pilot costs sign-ups without helping a method that keeps learning. Ten pulls still gave each arm 1,000 visitors.

We then checked the two assumptions our next step relies on: is the batch-to-batch noise binomial, and did any arm drift between its first and last pulls?

164def complete(self, result):
165    row = normalize_result(result)
166    with self.connection:
167        request = self.pending
168        if request is None or (int(row["Arm"]), row["Pull"]) != (
169                request["arm"], request["expected_pull"]):
170            raise ValueError("Response does not match the pending request")
171        previous = self.connection.execute('SELECT net_reward FROM results WHERE pull=?',
172                                           (row['Pull']-1,)).fetchone()
173        if (previous is not None and row['NetReward'] != previous[0]+row['Reward']) or (
174                row['Pull'] == 0 and row['NetReward'] != row['Reward']):
175            raise ValueError('Response cumulative reward does not match saved history')
176        inserted = self._insert(row, request["model"], request["parameters"], request["request_id"])
177        self.connection.execute("DELETE FROM pending WHERE singleton=1")
178    return inserted
phase1/main.py · noise_ratio · lines 293–302
293def noise_ratio(by_arm):
294    """Observed batch variance over the binomial variance; about 1 if batches are binomial."""
295    observed, expected, df = 0.0, 0.0, 0
296    for rewards in by_arm:
297        if len(rewards) >= 2:
298            rate = mean(rewards) / VISITORS_PER_PULL
299            observed += (len(rewards) - 1) * variance(rewards)
300            expected += (len(rewards) - 1) * VISITORS_PER_PULL * rate * (1 - rate)
301            df += len(rewards) - 1
302    return (observed / expected, df) if expected else (None, 0)
phase1/main.py · stability · lines 305–317
305def stability(by_arm):
306    """Standardized change from each arm's first half of pulls to its last half."""
307    scores, shift, spread = [], 0.0, 0.0
308    for rewards in by_arm:
309        half = len(rewards) // 2
310        rate = mean(rewards) / VISITORS_PER_PULL if rewards else 0
311        if half >= 2 and 0 < rate < 1:
312            change = mean(rewards[-half:]) - mean(rewards[:half])
313            error = 2 * VISITORS_PER_PULL * rate * (1 - rate) / half
314            scores.append(change / math.sqrt(error))
315            shift += change
316            spread += error
317    return scores, (shift / math.sqrt(spread) if spread else None)

report/build_report.py · arm_summary · lines 226–233
226def arm_summary(part, draws=400_000):
227    """Pulls, sign-ups, rate, Beta(1 + sign-ups, 1 + non-sign-ups) 95% interval and P(best) per arm."""
228    g = part.groupby("arm")["reward"].agg(pulls="size", signups="sum").reindex(range(K), fill_value=0)
229    a, b = 1 + g["signups"], 1 + V * g["pulls"] - g["signups"]
230    g["rate"] = g["signups"] / (V * g["pulls"])
231    g["low"], g["high"] = stats.beta.ppf(0.025, a, b), stats.beta.ppf(0.975, a, b)
232    g["p_best"] = prob_best(a.to_numpy(float), b.to_numpy(float), draws)
233    return g
report/build_report.py · prob_best · lines 216–223
216def prob_best(a, b, draws=400_000, seed=SEED):
217    """Share of joint Beta posterior draws in which each arm has the highest rate."""
218    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
219    wins = np.zeros(len(a))
220    for done in range(0, draws, 50_000):
221        size = min(50_000, draws - done)
222        wins += np.bincount(rng.beta(a, b, size=(size, len(a))).argmax(axis=1), minlength=len(a))
223    return wins / draws
What we learned
  • Arm 21 led at 25.5% (95% interval 22.9% to 28.3%), with a 93.0% chance of being the best arm.
  • Arms 0, 12, 5, 16 (21.3% to 22.0%) still had a small chance of being best, so our method needed to keep testing them.
  • Noise was close to binomial and no arm drifted unusually, so in Step 2 we could model each arm with a Beta posterior and a fixed rate.

Step 2: simulate the rest of the budget from the pilotOffline · 0 pulls

We turned the pilot into plausible "worlds" and played every candidate out to 1,000,000 pulls in each. We gave each arm a Beta(1 + sign-ups, 1 + non-sign-ups) distribution from its pilot result, and each world draws one true rate per arm from these distributions. We used 200 worlds. Each combination is a number of uniform pulls per arm (10, which is the pilot itself, or a top-up to 25, 50 or 100), followed by UCB (8 bonus multipliers), ε-greedy (5 values of ε) or Thompson Sampling: 56 combinations in all. We ran every combination on the same worlds, so the differences between them come from the method rather than from luck. We scored each one by the sign-ups it lost against always pulling that world's true best arm. Because the best of 56 on the same worlds looks better than it really is, we reran the top 5, plus each method's best, on 200 fresh worlds.

phase2/simulate.py · posterior · lines 17–21the pilot becomes a Beta posterior for each arm
17def posterior(pulls, signups, prior=(1.0, 1.0)):
18    """Beta(prior_a + sign-ups, prior_b + non-sign-ups) for each arm."""
19    pulls = np.asarray(pulls, float)
20    signups = np.asarray(signups, float)
21    return prior[0] + signups, prior[1] + V * pulls - signups
phase2/simulate.py · draw_worlds · lines 24–26one world = one true rate per arm
24def draw_worlds(a, b, reps, seed, stream):
25    """reps x K true rates. Each stream is an independent set of worlds."""
26    return np.random.default_rng([seed, stream]).beta(a, b, size=(reps, K))
phase2/simulate.py · run_policy · lines 49–133UCB, ε-greedy and Thompson Sampling, one pull at a time
 49def run_policy(kind, param, P, n, s, start, horizon, rng, trace=False, prior=(1.0, 1.0)):
 50    """Simulate pulls start..horizon-1 one at a time. Lane i uses param[i].
 51
 52    kind 'ucb': pull argmax of mean + param * sqrt(2 ln t / n), with t the pulls
 53                made so far. This is program/bandit's UCBModel with
 54                exploration = 2 * param**2. Ties go to the lowest arm.
 55    kind 'eps': with probability param, pull a uniformly random arm (any of the
 56                24); otherwise pull the arm with the highest mean.
 57    kind 'ts':  Thompson Sampling. Draw one rate from every arm's
 58                Beta(prior_a + sign-ups, prior_b + non-sign-ups) and pull the
 59                highest draw. param is ignored.
 60    """
 61    lanes = len(P)
 62    n, s = n.astype(float), s.astype(float)
 63    mu = s / (V * n)
 64    nf, sf, mf, Pf = n.reshape(-1), s.reshape(-1), mu.reshape(-1), P.reshape(-1)
 65    base = np.arange(lanes) * K
 66    param = np.asarray(param, float)
 67    if kind == 'ucb':
 68        isq = 1 / np.sqrt(n)
 69        qf = isq.reshape(-1)
 70        coef = (param * math.sqrt(2))[:, None]
 71    elif kind == 'ts':
 72        beta_a, beta_b = prior[0] + s, prior[1] + V * n - s
 73        af, bf = beta_a.reshape(-1), beta_b.reshape(-1)
 74    elif kind != 'eps':
 75        raise ValueError(kind)
 76
 77    best = P.max(axis=1)
 78    sum_p = np.zeros(lanes)
 79    marks = checkpoints(start, horizon)
 80    curve = np.zeros((len(marks), lanes))
 81    mark = 0
 82    log = {'arms': [], 'rewards': []} if trace else None
 83
 84    t = start
 85    while t < horizon:
 86        steps = min(CHUNK, horizon - t)
 87        if kind == 'eps':
 88            explore = rng.random((steps, lanes)) < param
 89            random_arm = rng.integers(0, K, (steps, lanes))
 90        for i in range(steps):
 91            if kind == 'ucb':
 92                arms = (mu + coef * math.sqrt(math.log(t)) * isq).argmax(axis=1)
 93            elif kind == 'ts':
 94                arms = rng.beta(beta_a, beta_b).argmax(axis=1)
 95            else:
 96                arms = np.where(explore[i], random_arm[i], mu.argmax(axis=1))
 97            flat = base + arms
 98            p = Pf[flat]
 99            sum_p += p
100            reward = rng.binomial(V, p)
101            pulls = nf[flat] + 1
102            nf[flat] = pulls
103            total = sf[flat] + reward
104            sf[flat] = total
105            mf[flat] = total / (V * pulls)
106            if kind == 'ucb':
107                qf[flat] = 1 / np.sqrt(pulls)
108            elif kind == 'ts':
109                af[flat] = prior[0] + total
110                bf[flat] = prior[1] + V * pulls - total
111            if trace:
112                log['arms'].append(int(arms[0]))
113                log['rewards'].append(int(reward[0]))
114            t += 1
115            if mark < len(marks) and t == marks[mark]:
116                curve[mark] = V * (best * (t - start) - sum_p)
117                mark += 1
118
119    lane = np.arange(lanes)
120    pick = mu.argmax(axis=1)
121    true_best = P.argmax(axis=1)
122    out = dict(
123        sum_p=sum_p,
124        pick=pick,
125        correct=pick == true_best,
126        pick_gap=V * (best - P[lane, pick]),
127        best_share=n[lane, true_best] / n.sum(axis=1),
128        marks=marks,
129        curve=curve,
130    )
131    if trace:
132        out['trace'] = log
133    return out

Our decision: UCB ×0.05, starting straight from the pilot. Thompson Sampling was best on the fresh worlds (542 ± 83 lost) and UCB ×0.05 came second, 836 ± 114 sign-ups behind. That gap is about 0.003% of the total, while luck alone moves the live total by about ±4,301 (one standard deviation), so the difference between the two would not have been visible in our result. We chose UCB ×0.05 because:
  • It is the model we had already built and tested in program/bandit, which our live driver uses. Switching to Thompson Sampling would have meant running new, untested code on a budget that cannot be redone.
  • UCB has no randomness, so every choice can be replayed from our saved data and explained. We replay all of them in the Results section.
  • Its worst world lost only 7,783. UCB ×0.02 had a similar mean but lost 447,523 in its worst world.
  • UCB is part of the course content; Thompson Sampling is not.
What we learned
  • We should start the method straight from the pilot: topping up to 100 pulls per arm cost about 21,000 more sign-ups, whichever method followed.
  • The lecture's UCB1 bonus (×1) lost about 719,000 and the best ε-greedy setting about 104,000, far behind scaled UCB and Thompson Sampling.
  • These figures are simulated. They assume binomial noise and fixed rates, which we had to confirm at the live checkpoints.

Step 3: staged live run with UCB ×0.05Live · 15,815 pulls

Our live method, UCB, gives each arm an optimistic score (its mean rate plus a bonus) and pulls the arm with the highest score:

score = mean rate + 0.05 × √(2 ln t ÷ n)

Here t is the total number of pulls so far and n is that arm's pulls. The bonus shrinks as an arm is pulled, so a rarely pulled arm gets another look only while its score can still beat the leader's. In our code this is UCBModel(exploration=0.005), because exploration = 2 × 0.05². Because we tuned the ×0.05 multiplier by simulation, we treat the score as an optimistic score rather than a calibrated confidence bound.

We started straight from the pilot data and stopped at two checkpoints to review the results before spending more: 1,200 pulls on 10 November and 5,000 on 11 November. We then made several shorter runs to measure and improve the request speed. We stopped one of them by hand at pull 15,054 while a request was in flight; our next run recovered that exact request (same arm, counter and request ID) before making any new choice. A final 1,000-pull run timed the driver with tuning switched on.

Code
program/bandit/models.py · UCBModel · lines 60–90the score and the choice
60class UCBModel(UniformModel):
61    """Batch-reward UCB; each pull's bounded reward is Reward / 100."""
62
63    name = "ucb"
64
65    def __init__(self, exploration=2.0):
66        if (isinstance(exploration, bool) or not isinstance(exploration, (int, float))
67                or not math.isfinite(exploration) or exploration <= 0):
68            raise ValueError("exploration must be finite and positive")
69        super().__init__()
70        self.exploration = float(exploration)
71
72    @property
73    def parameters(self):
74        return {"exploration": self.exploration}
75
76    def _score(self, arm):
77        count = self.counts[arm]
78        if not count:
79            return float("inf")
80        mean = self.signups[arm] / (VISITORS_PER_PULL * count)
81        return mean + math.sqrt(self.exploration * math.log(self.total_pulls) / count)
82
83    def select_arm(self):
84        return max(range(ARMS), key=lambda arm: (self._score(arm), -arm))
85
86    def summary(self):
87        rows = super().summary()
88        for row in rows:
89            row["score"] = self._score(row["arm"]) if row["pulls"] else None
90        return rows

program/bandit/runner.py · _resolve · lines 49–94an uncertain request is retried with the same identity until it resolves
49def _resolve(store, client, log, max_retries, *, fresh=False, stop=None):
50    request = store.pending
51    attempt = 0
52    while True:
53        attempt += 1
54        if stop:
55            stop.check()
56        log.write("pull_attempt", attempt=attempt, request=request)
57        try:
58            def before_send():
59                if stop and stop.is_set():
60                    if fresh and attempt == 1:
61                        store._cancel_unsent(request['request_id'])
62                    raise StopRequested()
63                if fresh and attempt == 1 and utc_now() >= DEADLINE:
64                    # The current call has not entered HTTP yet, so cancellation
65                    # is safe. Previously attempted/durable recoveries stay intact.
66                    store._cancel_unsent(request["request_id"])
67                    log.write("pull_cancelled", request=request, reason="deadline_reached")
68                    raise _DeadlineReached()
69
70            response = client.pull(request, before_send=before_send)
71            # Treat an invalid response as uncertain; do not abandon its identity.
72            try:
73                row = normalize_result(response)
74            except ValueError:
75                raise UncertainPullError(request["request_id"], request["expected_pull"]) from None
76            store.complete(row)
77            log.write("pull_completed", attempt=attempt, request=request, result=row)
78            return row
79        except UncertainPullError:
80            retry = max_retries is None or attempt <= max_retries
81            log.write("pull_uncertain", attempt=attempt, request=request,
82                      retry_scheduled=retry)
83            if stop:
84                stop.check()
85            if not retry:
86                raise
87            client.wait_before_retry()
88            if max_retries is None and attempt > 1:
89                delay = min(30., 2. ** min(attempt-1, 5))
90                if stop:
91                    if stop.wait(delay):
92                        raise StopRequested()
93                else:
94                    time.sleep(delay)

Step 4: continuous run with tuning checksLive · complete

From pull 16,055, a single driver ran continuously until the budget was used, sending one request at a time with at least 0.25 seconds between requests. It printed progress every 1,000 pulls, and a first Ctrl-C would have stopped it only after the in-flight response was saved.

Every 200,000 pulls, the driver paused for one to two minutes to recheck the multiplier. It simulated the whole remaining budget from the current posteriors, trying candidates from ×0.02 to ×0.10 for the next stage. We set it to switch only if a candidate was clearly better on expected loss over the remaining budget, no worse on next-stage loss and no worse on the average loss in the worst 5% of simulated worlds (CVaR 95%), and only if the improvement held up on a fresh set of simulated worlds. Otherwise it kept the current setting.

Checks 1 to 4 kept ×0.05. Check 5 at pull 816,055, with 183,945 pulls left, switched to ×0.02 for the rest of the run.

Code
program/bandit/tuning.py · evaluate · lines 211–261rank the candidates on simulated worlds
211def evaluate(stats, remaining, baseline, config):
212    import numpy as np
213    integer(remaining, 'remaining', maximum=MAX_PULLS)
214    from .models import UCBModel
215    model = UCBModel(round(2*baseline**2, 12)).fit_aggregates(stats)
216    n, s = np.array(model.counts), np.array(model.signups)
217    candidates = sorted(set((*config.candidates, baseline)))
218    stage = min(config.interval, remaining)
219    result = {'selected_multiplier': baseline, 'baseline_multiplier': baseline,
220              'horizon': remaining, 'stage_horizon': stage, 'reason': 'baseline_retained',
221              'continuation': 'current_multiplier_with_sequential_learning', 'candidates': []}
222    if not remaining or not np.all(n > 0):
223        result['reason'] = 'no_budget_or_unseen_arms'
224        return result
225    seed = config.seed + int(n.sum())
226    p, w = draw_worlds(n, s, config.train_worlds, seed)
227    sample = rollout(p, n, s, candidates, baseline, stage, remaining, seed+1)
228    leader = int((s/(100*n)).argmax())
229    wrong = p.argmax(axis=1) != leader
230    wrong_mass = float(w[wrong].sum()/w.sum())
231    for j, c in enumerate(candidates):
232        full, error, ess = _mean_error(sample['full'][j], w)
233        short = float(np.average(sample['stage'][j], weights=w))
234        result['candidates'].append({
235            'multiplier': c, 'expected_full_regret': full, 'expected_stage_regret': short,
236            'expected_full_signups': float(100*remaining*np.average(p.max(axis=1), weights=w)-full),
237            'expected_stage_signups': float(100*stage*np.average(p.max(axis=1), weights=w)-short),
238            'full_regret_mc_se': error, 'ess': ess,
239            'cvar': weighted_cvar(sample['full'][j], w, config.cvar_level),
240            'leader_wrong_probability': wrong_mass,
241            'regret_if_leader_wrong': float(np.average(sample['full'][j, wrong], weights=w[wrong]))
242                if w[wrong].sum() else None})
243    base = next(row for row in result['candidates'] if row['multiplier'] == baseline)
244    feasible = [row for row in result['candidates']
245                if row['expected_stage_regret'] <= base['expected_stage_regret']+config.stage_loss_allowance
246                and row['cvar'] <= base['cvar']+config.tail_loss_allowance]
247    chosen = min(feasible, key=lambda row: (row['expected_full_regret'], row['multiplier'] != baseline))
248    if chosen['multiplier'] == baseline:
249        return result
250    # Independent worlds AND independent observation noise, for one preselected challenger.
251    vp, vw = draw_worlds(n, s, config.validation_worlds, seed+1000003)
252    validation = rollout(vp, n, s, [chosen['multiplier'], baseline], baseline,
253                         stage, remaining, seed+1000004)
254    gate = validate_switch({k: validation[k][0] for k in ('full', 'stage')},
255                           {k: validation[k][1] for k in ('full', 'stage')}, vw, config)
256    result['validation'] = gate
257    result['proposed_multiplier'] = chosen['multiplier']
258    result['reason'] = gate['reason']
259    if gate['accepted']:
260        result['selected_multiplier'] = chosen['multiplier']
261    return result
program/bandit/tuning.py · validate_switch · lines 181–208a switch must pass every safeguard on fresh worlds
181def validate_switch(candidate, baseline, weights, config):
182    """Conservative Monte Carlo screening, NOT a distribution-free guarantee."""
183    import numpy as np
184    full, full_se, ess = _mean_error(candidate['full']-baseline['full'], weights)
185    short, short_se, _ = _mean_error(candidate['stage']-baseline['stage'], weights)
186    tail = weighted_cvar(candidate['full'], weights, config.cvar_level) - weighted_cvar(
187        baseline['full'], weights, config.cvar_level)
188    # Paired bootstrap of proposal draws; retain importance weights in each sample.
189    rng = np.random.default_rng(config.seed+12345)
190    differences = []
191    for _ in range(96):
192        ix = rng.integers(0, len(weights), len(weights))
193        if weights[ix].sum() <= 0:
194            return {'accepted': False, 'reason': 'insufficient_importance_mass'}
195        differences.append(weighted_cvar(candidate['full'][ix], weights[ix], config.cvar_level) -
196                           weighted_cvar(baseline['full'][ix], weights[ix], config.cvar_level))
197    tail_se = float(np.std(differences, ddof=1))
198    # At least a few effective tail draws; otherwise never claim tail safety.
199    tail_ess = min(_tail_ess(candidate['full'], weights, config.cvar_level),
200                   _tail_ess(baseline['full'], weights, config.cvar_level))
201    enough = ess >= config.min_ess and tail_ess >= 4
202    full_upper, short_upper, tail_upper = full+2.58*full_se, short+2.58*short_se, tail+2.58*tail_se
203    accepted = (enough and full_upper < -config.min_gain and
204                short_upper <= config.stage_loss_allowance and tail_upper <= config.tail_loss_allowance)
205    return {'accepted': bool(accepted), 'ess': ess, 'tail_ess': tail_ess, 'full_regret_difference': full,
206            'stage_regret_difference': short, 'cvar_difference': tail,
207            'full_difference_upper': full_upper, 'stage_difference_upper': short_upper,
208            'cvar_difference_upper': tail_upper, 'reason': 'validated' if accepted else 'safeguard_or_uncertainty'}

What we learned
  • Our simulated expected loss over the remaining budget fell from about 1,018 sign-ups at check 1 to about 44 at check 5, as our data separated arm 21 more clearly from the others at every stage.
  • At check 1, ×0.03 had a slightly lower expected loss than ×0.05 but a higher CVaR, so our safeguard kept ×0.05. Larger multipliers (×0.075 and ×0.10) would have explored more and lost more at every check.
  • At check 5, arm 21 was 6.1 standard errors ahead of arm 12 and only 183,945 pulls were left. Under the current model and remaining budget, simulations favoured reducing exploration to ×0.02. ×0.05 would still have spent a few pulls on the runners-up (about 44 sign-ups lost in expectation), whereas ×0.02 made their bonus too small to overtake arm 21. On fresh simulated worlds, ×0.02 lowered the expected loss by 51.5 sign-ups and CVaR by 167, so the switch passed every safeguard.
  • All of the 183,945 pulls after check 5 went to arm 21. The stage before it had put 13 of its 200,000 pulls elsewhere. Independent validation estimated an expected gain of 51.5 sign-ups from the switch.
  • The tuning checks are simulations based on our live data. We used them to support the choice of setting; they are not live results.

report/build_report.py · stage_table · lines 299–330
299def stage_table(df, tuning, leader, final):
300    """Pulls, sign-ups, conversion, share on the leader and speed for each stage of the live run.
301
302    Speed counts only gaps under 60 seconds between saved pulls, so pauses between runs and
303    tuning checks don't count as running time.
304    """
305    n = len(df)
306    starts = [d["at_pull"] for d in tuning] or [16_055]
307    blocks = [(0, PILOT_PULLS, "Pilot"),
308              (PILOT_PULLS, CHECKPOINTS[0], "Stage 1"),
309              (CHECKPOINTS[0], starts[0], "Stage 2")]
310    for i, start in enumerate(starts):
311        end = starts[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(starts) else n
312        label = "Stage 3.{}, after check {}".format(i + 1, i + 1)
313        blocks.append((start, end, label + (" (running)" if end == n and not final else "")))
314    by_arm = df.groupby("arm")["reward"]
315    rate = by_arm.sum() / (V * by_arm.size())
316    cost = V * (rate[leader] - rate.reindex(df["arm"]).to_numpy())  # Per pull, at the latest estimates
317    rows = []
318    for start, end, label in blocks:
319        part = df.iloc[start:min(end, n)]
320        if part.empty:
321            continue
322        gaps = part["time"].diff().dt.total_seconds().iloc[1:]
323        running = gaps[gaps < 60]
324        rows.append({"label": label, "first": start, "last": start + len(part) - 1, "pulls": len(part),
325                     "signups": int(part["reward"].sum()), "on_leader": float((part["arm"] == leader).mean()),
326                     "arms": int(part["arm"].nunique()), "method": method_label(part),
327                     "speed": len(running) / running.sum() if running.sum() else float("nan"),
328                     "cost": float(cost[start:start + len(part)].sum()),
329                     "start": part["time"].iloc[0], "end": part["time"].iloc[-1]})
330    return rows

Arm allocation

As evidence built up, the share of our pulls not on arm 21 fell steadily. UCB kept checking the runners-up, arms 12 and 0, while their scores could still overtake the leader's, and returned to them less and less often. After check 5 switched to ×0.02 at pull 816,055, every pull went to arm 21. The pilot, which pulled every arm evenly, is not shown.

Analysis code for this output: allocation_bins()
report/build_report.py · allocation_bins · lines 333–343
333def allocation_bins(df, leader, runners, bins=28):
334    """Share of pulls on each arm in log-spaced windows of the pull number, after the pilot."""
335    arms = df["arm"].to_numpy()
336    edges = np.unique(np.geomspace(PILOT_PULLS, len(df), bins + 1).astype(int))
337    rows = []
338    for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
339        window = arms[lo:hi]
340        row = {"lo": lo, "hi": hi, "mid": math.sqrt(lo * hi), "others": float((window != leader).mean())}
341        row.update({"arm{}".format(a): float((window == a).mean()) for a in runners})
342        rows.append(row)
343    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

Conversion

Our cumulative conversion rate climbed from the pilot's level towards arm 21's own rate, which is the most any method could achieve once arm 21 is known to be best. The windowed rate reached that level early and stayed there.

Analysis code for this output: conversion_bins()
report/build_report.py · conversion_bins · lines 346–357
346def conversion_bins(df, bins=32):
347    """Conversion rate in windows of the pull number, and the cumulative rate so far.
348
349    The pilot is one window; after it, windows are log-spaced.
350    """
351    rewards = df["reward"].to_numpy()
352    total = np.cumsum(rewards)
353    edges = np.unique(np.concatenate([[0], np.geomspace(PILOT_PULLS, len(df), bins).astype(int)]))
354    rows = [{"lo": lo, "hi": hi, "mid": math.sqrt(max(lo, 1) * hi),
355             "window": rewards[lo:hi].sum() / (V * (hi - lo)), "cumulative": total[hi - 1] / (V * hi)}
356            for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:])]
357    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

All 24 arms

Arm 21 received 99.88% of all our pulls. The runner-up by rate, arm 12, is 1.15 points behind (z = 6.1), so under a normal approximation the chance that it is actually better is less than one in a million. P(best) uses 200,000 joint draws from each arm's Beta posterior.

226def arm_summary(part, draws=400_000):
227    """Pulls, sign-ups, rate, Beta(1 + sign-ups, 1 + non-sign-ups) 95% interval and P(best) per arm."""
228    g = part.groupby("arm")["reward"].agg(pulls="size", signups="sum").reindex(range(K), fill_value=0)
229    a, b = 1 + g["signups"], 1 + V * g["pulls"] - g["signups"]
230    g["rate"] = g["signups"] / (V * g["pulls"])
231    g["low"], g["high"] = stats.beta.ppf(0.025, a, b), stats.beta.ppf(0.975, a, b)
232    g["p_best"] = prob_best(a.to_numpy(float), b.to_numpy(float), draws)
233    return g

Is the leading arm's rate stable?

Step 0 showed that changing rates were the main risk to our approach, so we split the run into 20 equal windows of the pull number and tested whether a single fixed rate explains arm 21's results in all of them.

Leading arm 21: 998,794 pulls, rate 24.454%.
Chi-square across the 20 windows: 23.4 on 19 degrees of freedom, p = 0.22 (a small p would mean the rate changed).
Batch dispersion: 0.998 times binomial (about 1 ± 0.003 is normal).
Phase 1 checks rerun on all 1,000,000 pulls: noise 0.998 times binomial; 1 of 24 arms moved by more than 2 standard errors between the first and second half of their pulls; all arms together -0.5.
Analysis code for this output: leader_stability()
report/build_report.py · leader_stability · lines 360–385
360def leader_stability(df, leader, blocks=20):
361    """Has the leader's rate drifted? Its rate in 20 equal windows of the pull number, plus two tests.
362
363    With the full budget each window is 50,000 pulls. Chi-square: are the windows' sign-up rates
364    consistent with one fixed rate? Dispersion: batch variance over the binomial variance
365    100 p (1 - p); about 1 if batches are binomial.
366    """
367    rows = df[df["arm"] == leader]
368    rewards, pulls = rows["reward"].to_numpy(), rows["pull"].to_numpy()
369    edges = np.linspace(0, len(df), blocks + 1).astype(int)
370    out = []
371    for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
372        inside = (pulls >= lo) & (pulls < hi)
373        s, n = int(rewards[inside].sum()), int(inside.sum())
374        if n == 0:
375            continue
376        rate = s / (V * n)
377        half = 1.96 * math.sqrt(rate * (1 - rate) / (V * n))
378        out.append({"first": int(lo), "last": int(hi) - 1, "pulls": n, "signups": s,
379                    "rate": rate, "low": rate - half, "high": rate + half})
380    out = pd.DataFrame(out)
381    chi2, p_value, dof, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(np.column_stack([out["signups"], V * out["pulls"] - out["signups"]]))
382    p = rewards.sum() / (V * len(rewards))
383    dispersion = rewards.var(ddof=1) / (V * p * (1 - p))
384    return out, {"chi2": chi2, "dof": dof, "p_value": p_value, "dispersion": dispersion,
385                 "tolerance": 2 * math.sqrt(2 / (len(rewards) - 1)), "rate": p}

255def replay_ucb(df):
256    """Re-make every saved UCB choice from the pulls before it, with UCBModel's score and tie-break.
257
258    Score = mean + sqrt(exploration * ln(total pulls) / arm pulls). The highest score wins and
259    ties go to the lowest arm, as in program/bandit/models.py. Each pull uses its saved exploration.
260    """
261    arms, rewards = df["arm"].to_numpy(), df["reward"].to_numpy()
262    exploration, is_ucb = df["exploration"].to_numpy(), (df["model"] == "ucb").to_numpy()
263    counts, signups, means = [0] * K, [0] * K, [0.0] * K
264    checked = mismatched = 0
265    first = None
266    for i in range(len(arms)):
267        if is_ucb[i]:
268            scale = float(exploration[i]) * math.log(i)  # i pulls were saved before this one
269            best, best_score = 0, -math.inf
270            for arm in range(K):
271                c = counts[arm]
272                score = math.inf if c == 0 else means[arm] + math.sqrt(scale / c)
273                if score > best_score:
274                    best, best_score = arm, score
275            checked += 1
276            if best != arms[i]:
277                mismatched += 1
278                first = i if first is None else first
279        arm = int(arms[i])
280        counts[arm] += 1
281        signups[arm] += int(rewards[i])
282        means[arm] = signups[arm] / (V * counts[arm])
283    return {"checked": checked, "mismatched": mismatched, "first_mismatch": first}

Our final result

We used all 1,000,000 pulls and recorded 24,449,708 sign-ups from 100,000,000 visitors, an overall conversion rate of 24.45%. We choose arm 21. Its conversion rate is 24.454% (95% interval 24.445% to 24.462%) over 998,794 pulls, and its posterior probability of being the best arm is >99.99%. The closest alternative, arm 12, is 1.15 percentage points behind (z = 6.1). Compared with sending every pull to arm 21 from the start, our approach gave up an estimated 3,985 sign-ups (0.016% of the total), 2,108 of them in the 240-pull pilot.

Appendix A: LLM use and prompts

We used Claude Code (VS Code extension) with Claude Opus 5.5 as a coding and analysis assistant. We used it to write and review our simulators and live drivers, run the local simulations, help us interpret results, and draft documentation and this file. We made the decisions on the method, its settings and when to spend pulls ourselves. Our prompts come from 10 Claude Code sessions between 30 October and 14 November 2026, 110 prompts in total.

For each project step below, we summarise what we asked the LLM to do and list representative prompts. We have edited these prompts for spelling, grammar and clarity; the substance of each request is unchanged, and our original prompts are available on request. Where we included group notes in a prompt, we describe them in brackets instead of repeating them. None of our prompts contains our group password.

  1"""Offline bandit simulator for DBA5101 GP3.
  2
  3Entirely local: this file does not import server_pull and opens no network
  4connections. Every conversion rate here is invented, so results describe how
  5methods behave across plausible worlds, not what the live server contains.

  7Usage:
  8    python simulate.py bench
  9    python simulate.py validate

 12import argparse
 13import csv
 14import math
 15import os
 16import sys
 17import time
 18from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, as_completed
 19
 20import numpy as np
 21
 22K = 24
 23V = 100  # Visitors per pull.
 24T = 1_000_000
 25RESULTS = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), 'results')
 26CURVE_POINTS = np.unique(np.geomspace(2_400, T, 40).astype(int))

 28
 29# ---------------------------------------------------------------- worlds
 30def _wide(rng):
 31    return rng.uniform(.08, .22, K)
 32
 33
 34def _factorial(rng):
 35    # Four buttons x six media, with additive effects and small interactions.
 36    button = rng.normal(0, .012, 4)
 37    media = rng.normal(0, .012, 6)
 38    rates = .12 + (button[:, None] + media[None, :]).ravel() + rng.normal(0, .002, K)
 39    return np.clip(rates, .01, .5)
 40
 41
 42def _clear(rng):
 43    rates = rng.uniform(.12, .16, K)
 44    rates[rng.integers(K)] = .20
 45    return rates
 46
 47
 48def _close(rng):
 49    rates = rng.uniform(.12, .19, K)
 50    rates[rng.permutation(K)[:3]] = [.20, .199, .197]
 51    return rates
 52
 53
 54SCENARIOS = {
 55    'wide': dict(gen=_wide),
 56    'factorial': dict(gen=_factorial),
 57    'clear_winner': dict(gen=_clear),
 58    'close_race': dict(gen=_close),
 59    'extra_noise': dict(gen=_factorial, batch_sd=.03),
 60    'rates_change': dict(gen=_wide, change_at=400_000),
 61    'gap7': dict(fixed=(.22, .15)),
 62    'gap2': dict(fixed=(.22, .20)),
 63}
 64SCENARIO_ID = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(SCENARIOS)}
 65
 66
 67def make_worlds(name, reps):
 68    """Same reps give the same worlds for every method, so comparisons are paired."""
 69    spec = SCENARIOS[name]
 70    P0, P1 = np.zeros((reps, K)), None
 71    if spec.get('change_at'):
 72        P1 = np.zeros((reps, K))
 73    for rep in range(reps):
 74        rng = np.random.default_rng([1000, SCENARIO_ID[name], rep])
 75        if 'fixed' in spec:
 76            P0[rep] = spec['fixed'][1]
 77            P0[rep, rng.integers(K)] = spec['fixed'][0]
 78        else:
 79            P0[rep] = spec['gen'](rng)
 80        if P1 is not None:
 81            # The best arm fades and a formerly ordinary arm overtakes it.
 82            old_best = P0[rep].argmax()
 83            riser = rng.choice(np.delete(np.arange(K), old_best))
 84            P1[rep] = P0[rep]
 85            P1[rep, old_best] -= .04
 86            P1[rep, riser] = P0[rep, old_best] + .015
 87    return P0, P1, spec.get('change_at'), spec.get('batch_sd', 0.0)
 88
 89
 90def draw(rng, p, batch_sd):
 91    if batch_sd:
 92        p = np.clip(p + rng.normal(0, batch_sd, np.shape(p)), 0, 1)
 93    return rng.binomial(V, p)
 94
 95
 96def run_pilot(name, P0, batch_sd, n0):
 97    """The same uniform sample for each method, with n0 pulls on every arm."""
 98    rng = np.random.default_rng([2000, SCENARIO_ID[name], n0])
 99    reps = len(P0)
100    s = draw(rng, np.repeat(P0[:, :, None], n0, axis=2), batch_sd).sum(axis=2).astype(float)
101    return np.full((reps, K), float(n0)), s

103
104# --------------------------------------------------------------- metrics
105def stated_confidence(mu, n, rng, draws=2000):
106    """Posterior probability that the arm with the highest average is best."""
107    out = np.zeros(len(mu))
108    picks = mu.argmax(axis=1)
109    sd = np.sqrt(mu * (1 - mu) / (V * n))
110    for rep in range(len(mu)):
111        sample = mu[rep] + sd[rep] * rng.standard_normal((draws, K))
112        out[rep] = (sample.argmax(axis=1) == picks[rep]).mean()
113    return out
114
115
116def finish(regret, mu, n, P_end, rng, curve=None):
117    picks = mu.argmax(axis=1)
118    idx = np.arange(len(mu))
119    best_end = P_end.max(axis=1)
120    return dict(
121        regret=regret,
122        correct=(P_end[idx, picks] == best_end).astype(float),
123        final_gap=V * (best_end - P_end[idx, picks]),
124        confidence=stated_confidence(mu, n, rng),
125        curve=curve,
126    )
127
128
129# -------------------------------------------------------------- policies
130def run_explore_first(N, P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, rng, horizon=T):
131    """Exact closed form: exploitation has no decisions left to simulate."""
132    n, s = n0.copy(), s0.copy()
133    extra = N - int(n0[0, 0])
134    if extra > 0:
135        s += draw(rng, np.repeat(P0[:, :, None], extra, axis=2), batch_sd).sum(axis=2)
136        n += extra
137    t0 = int(n.sum(axis=1)[0])
138    mu = s / (V * n)
139    picks = mu.argmax(axis=1)
140    idx = np.arange(len(P0))
141    regret = V * ((P0.max(axis=1, keepdims=True) - P0) * n).sum(axis=1)
142    if P1 is None:
143        regret += V * (horizon - t0) * (P0.max(axis=1) - P0[idx, picks])
144        P_end = P0
145    else:
146        regret += V * (change_at - t0) * (P0.max(axis=1) - P0[idx, picks])
147        regret += V * (horizon - change_at) * (P1.max(axis=1) - P1[idx, picks])
148        P_end = P1
149    curve = np.full(len(CURVE_POINTS), np.nan)
150    for i, t in enumerate(CURVE_POINTS):
151        if t >= t0 and P1 is None:
152            done = V * ((P0.max(axis=1, keepdims=True) - P0) * n).sum(axis=1)
153            curve[i] = (done + V * (t - t0) * (P0.max(axis=1) - P0[idx, picks])).mean()
154    return finish(regret, mu, n, P_end, rng, curve)
155
156
157def run_loop(cfg, P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, rng, horizon=T):
158    """One pull at a time, vectorised across replications."""
159    reps = len(P0)
160    idx = np.arange(reps)
161    kind = cfg['kind']
162    n, s = n0.copy(), s0.copy()
163    mu = s / (V * n)
164    P = P0
165    best = P.max(axis=1)
166    regret = V * ((best[:, None] - P) * n).sum(axis=1)
167    isq = 1 / np.sqrt(n)
168    sd = np.sqrt(mu * (1 - mu) / (V * n))
169    points = {int(t): i for i, t in enumerate(CURVE_POINTS)}
170    curve = np.full(len(CURVE_POINTS), np.nan)
171    t0 = int(n.sum(axis=1)[0])
172    c = cfg.get('c', 0.0)
173    eps = cfg.get('eps', 0.0)
174
175    for t in range(t0 + 1, horizon + 1):
176        if change_at == t:
177            P = P1
178            best = P.max(axis=1)
179
180        if kind == 'ucb':
181            arms = (mu + c * math.sqrt(2 * math.log(t)) * isq).argmax(axis=1)
182        elif kind == 'ts':
183            arms = (mu + sd * rng.standard_normal((reps, K))).argmax(axis=1)
184        elif kind == 'ts_exact':
185            arms = rng.beta(1 + s, 1 + V * n - s).argmax(axis=1)
186        else:
187            rate = eps if kind == 'eps' else min(1.0, c * K / t)
188            arms = mu.argmax(axis=1)
189            explore = rng.random(reps) < rate
190            count = explore.sum()
191            if count:
192                arms[explore] = rng.integers(0, K, count)
193
194        p = P[idx, arms]
195        rewards = draw(rng, p, batch_sd)
196        regret += V * (best - p)
197        new_n = n[idx, arms] + 1
198        new_s = s[idx, arms] + rewards
199        new_mu = new_s / (V * new_n)
200        n[idx, arms] = new_n
201        s[idx, arms] = new_s
202        mu[idx, arms] = new_mu
203        if kind == 'ucb':
204            isq[idx, arms] = 1 / np.sqrt(new_n)
205        elif kind == 'ts':
206            sd[idx, arms] = np.sqrt(new_mu * (1 - new_mu) / (V * new_n))
207        if t in points:
208            curve[points[t]] = regret.mean()
209
210    return finish(regret, mu, n, P if P1 is None else P1, rng, curve)
211
212
213def label_of(cfg):
214    kind = cfg['kind']
215    if kind == 'explore_first':
216        return f"Explore-first N={cfg['N']}"
217    if kind == 'eps':
218        return f"Fixed e-greedy e={cfg['eps']:g}"
219    if kind == 'adaptive':
220        return f"Adaptive e-greedy c={cfg['c']:g}"
221    if kind == 'ucb':
222        return 'UCB1 slide bonus' if cfg['c'] == 1 else f"UCB1 bonus x{cfg['c']:g}"
223    return 'Thompson Sampling'
224
225
226def execute(cfg, P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, rng, horizon=T):
227    if cfg['kind'] == 'explore_first':
228        return run_explore_first(cfg['N'], P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, rng, horizon)
229    return run_loop(cfg, P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, rng, horizon)
230
231
232# ---------------------------------------------------------- staged plan
233def staged_plan(name, N0, budget, rule, reps=1000):
234    """Initial uniform pulls, then rounds of 50 extra pulls per contender."""
235    P, _, _, _ = make_worlds(name, reps)
236    rng = np.random.default_rng([3000, SCENARIO_ID[name], N0, budget, len(rule)])
237    idx = np.arange(reps)
238    first = rng.binomial(V, np.repeat(P[:, :, None], N0, axis=2)).astype(float)
239    s, ss = first.sum(axis=2), (first ** 2).sum(axis=2)
240    n = np.full((reps, K), float(N0))
241    used = np.full(reps, float(N0 * K))
242    active = np.ones(reps, bool)
243
244    def contenders():
245        mu = s / (V * n)
246        leader = mu.argmax(axis=1)
247        var = V * mu * (1 - mu)
248        lead_mu = mu[idx, leader][:, None]
249        lead_var = var[idx, leader][:, None]
250        lead_n = n[idx, leader][:, None]
251        keep = V * (lead_mu - mu) <= 2 * np.sqrt(lead_var / lead_n + var / n)
252        if rule == 'uniform':
253            keep = np.ones_like(keep)
254        elif rule == 'close_and_high_variance':
255            sample_var = (ss - s ** 2 / n) / (n - 1)
256            masked = np.where(keep, sample_var, np.nan)
257            keep = keep & (sample_var >= np.nanmedian(masked, axis=1, keepdims=True))
258            keep[idx, leader] = True
259        return keep
260
261    keep = contenders()
262    while budget > N0 * K:
263        size = keep.sum(axis=1)
264        active &= (used + 50 * size <= budget) & (size > 1)
265        if not active.any():
266            break
267        mask = keep & active[:, None]
268        if rule == 'close_and_high_variance':
269            extra = rng.binomial(V, np.repeat(P[:, :, None], 50, axis=2)).astype(float)
270            s += extra.sum(axis=2) * mask
271            ss += (extra ** 2).sum(axis=2) * mask
272        else:
273            s += rng.binomial(50 * V, P) * mask
274        n += 50 * mask
275        used += 50 * size * active
276        keep = contenders()
277
278    mu = s / (V * n)
279    picks = mu.argmax(axis=1)
280    best = P.max(axis=1)
281    best_arm = P.argmax(axis=1)
282    gap = V * (best - P[idx, picks])
283    regret = V * ((best[:, None] - P) * n).sum(axis=1) + (T - used) * gap
284    return dict(
285        scenario=name, N0=N0, budget=budget, rule=rule,
286        pulls_used=used.mean(), leader_is_best=(picks == best_arm).mean(),
287        best_still_contender=keep[idx, best_arm].mean(),
288        mean_gap=gap.mean(), mean_regret=regret.mean(),
289        p95_regret=np.percentile(regret, 95),
290    )
291
292
293# ---------------------------------------------------------------- jobs
294def job_method(exp, scenario, cfg, N0, reps, index):
295    P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd = make_worlds(scenario, reps)
296    n0, s0 = run_pilot(scenario, P0, batch_sd, N0)
297    rng = np.random.default_rng([4000, SCENARIO_ID[scenario], index, N0])
298    out = execute(cfg, P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, rng)
299    return dict(exp=exp, scenario=scenario, label=label_of(cfg), kind=cfg['kind'], N0=N0, **out)
300
301
302def job_rehearsal(scenario, cfg, world_kind, reps, index):
303    """Predict a method's regret from a pilot, using truth, plug-in or posterior rates."""
304    P_true, _, _, _ = make_worlds(scenario, reps)
305    n0, s0 = run_pilot(scenario, P_true, 0.0, 100)
306    if world_kind == 'truth':
307        P = P_true
308    elif world_kind == 'plug_in':
309        P = s0 / (V * n0)
310    else:
311        rate_rng = np.random.default_rng([5000, SCENARIO_ID[scenario]])
312        P = rate_rng.beta(1 + s0, 1 + V * n0 - s0)
313    rng = np.random.default_rng([6000, SCENARIO_ID[scenario], index, len(world_kind)])
314    out = execute(cfg, P, None, None, 0.0, n0, s0, rng)
315    return dict(exp='rehearsal', scenario=scenario, label=label_of(cfg), kind=cfg['kind'],
316                N0=100, world=world_kind, **out)
317
318
319METHODS = (
320    [dict(kind='explore_first', N=N) for N in (100, 500, 2000, 10000)]
321    + [dict(kind='eps', eps=e) for e in (.1, .01, .001)]
322    + [dict(kind='adaptive', c=c) for c in (10, 100, 1000)]
323    + [dict(kind='ucb', c=c) for c in (1, .2, .05, .02)]
324    + [dict(kind='ts')]
325)
326MAIN_SCENARIOS = ('wide', 'factorial', 'clear_winner', 'close_race', 'extra_noise', 'rates_change')
327ROW_FIELDS = ['exp', 'scenario', 'label', 'kind', 'N0', 'world', 'rep', 'regret',
328              'correct', 'final_gap', 'confidence']
329
330
331def run_all(reps):
332    os.makedirs(RESULTS, exist_ok=True)
333    jobs = []
334    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 3) - 2)) as pool:
335        index = 0
336        for scenario in MAIN_SCENARIOS:
337            for cfg in METHODS:
338                index += 1
339                jobs.append(pool.submit(job_method, 'main', scenario, cfg, 100, reps, index))
340        for scenario in ('gap7', 'gap2'):
341            for cfg in (dict(kind='eps', eps=.1), dict(kind='ucb', c=1),
342                        dict(kind='ucb', c=.05), dict(kind='ts')):
343                index += 1
344                jobs.append(pool.submit(job_method, 'hand_check', scenario, cfg, 100, 20, index))
345        for scenario in ('wide', 'factorial', 'close_race'):
346            for cfg in (dict(kind='ucb', c=.05), dict(kind='ts')):
347                for N0 in (1, 400):
348                    index += 1
349                    jobs.append(pool.submit(job_method, 'pilot_size', scenario, cfg, N0, reps, index))
350        for scenario in ('factorial', 'close_race'):
351            for cfg in (dict(kind='explore_first', N=100), dict(kind='ucb', c=.05), dict(kind='ts')):
352                for world in ('truth', 'plug_in', 'posterior'):
353                    index += 1
354                    jobs.append(pool.submit(job_rehearsal, scenario, cfg, world, reps, index))
355
356        staged = []
357        for scenario in ('wide', 'factorial', 'clear_winner', 'close_race'):
358            for rule in ('uniform', 'close_to_leader', 'close_and_high_variance'):
359                for N0 in (50, 100, 200):
360                    for budget in (N0 * K, 5000, 10000):
361                        staged.append(pool.submit(staged_plan, scenario, N0, budget, rule))
362
363        start = time.time()
364        with open(os.path.join(RESULTS, 'runs.csv'), 'w', newline='') as f_runs, \
365                open(os.path.join(RESULTS, 'curves.csv'), 'w', newline='') as f_curves:
366            runs = csv.DictWriter(f_runs, ROW_FIELDS)
367            runs.writeheader()
368            curves = csv.writer(f_curves)
369            curves.writerow(['exp', 'scenario', 'label', 'N0', 'world', 'pull', 'mean_regret'])
370            for done, future in enumerate(as_completed(jobs), 1):
371                res = future.result()
372                world = res.get('world', '')
373                for rep in range(len(res['regret'])):
374                    runs.writerow(dict(
375                        exp=res['exp'], scenario=res['scenario'], label=res['label'], kind=res['kind'],
376                        N0=res['N0'], world=world, rep=rep, regret=f"{res['regret'][rep]:.1f}",
377                        correct=int(res['correct'][rep]), final_gap=f"{res['final_gap'][rep]:.4f}",
378                        confidence=f"{res['confidence'][rep]:.4f}"))
379                for t, value in zip(CURVE_POINTS, res['curve']):
380                    if not np.isnan(value):
381                        curves.writerow([res['exp'], res['scenario'], res['label'], res['N0'], world,
382                                         int(t), f'{value:.1f}'])
383                f_runs.flush()
384                f_curves.flush()
385                print(f"[{done}/{len(jobs)}] {time.time() - start:6.0f}s {res['exp']} "
386                      f"{res['scenario']} {res['label']} {world}", flush=True)
387
388        rows = [future.result() for future in staged]
389        with open(os.path.join(RESULTS, 'staged_plan.csv'), 'w', newline='') as f_staged:
390            writer = csv.DictWriter(f_staged, list(rows[0]))
391            writer.writeheader()
392            writer.writerows(rows)
393        print(f'Finished in {time.time() - start:.0f}s', flush=True)
394

397def bench(reps):
398    P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd = make_worlds('factorial', reps)
399    n0, s0 = run_pilot('factorial', P0, batch_sd, 100)
400    for cfg in (dict(kind='eps', eps=.01), dict(kind='ucb', c=.05), dict(kind='ts')):
401        start = time.time()
402        run_loop(cfg, P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, np.random.default_rng(1), horizon=22_400)
403        per_pull = (time.time() - start) / 20_000
404        print(f"{cfg['kind']:>4}: {per_pull * 1e6:6.1f} us per pull, "
405              f"{per_pull * T:5.0f}s per 1M-pull run at {reps} reps")

408def validate():
409    """Check the simulator against results that can be worked out by hand."""
410    # Fixed 10% exploration costs eps * (23/24) * gap on every pull.
411    P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd = make_worlds('gap7', 40)
412    n0, s0 = run_pilot('gap7', P0, batch_sd, 100)
413    horizon = 102_400
414    out = run_loop(dict(kind='eps', eps=.1), P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0,
415                   np.random.default_rng(1), horizon)
416    pilot = 7 * 100 * 23
417    expected = pilot + .1 * (23 / 24) * 7 * (horizon - 2400)
418    print(f'e-greedy regret: simulated {out["regret"].mean():,.0f}, formula {expected:,.0f}')
419
420    # With both arms uniformly sampled, P(wrong) follows from a normal approximation.
421    rng = np.random.default_rng(2)
422    for gap, formula in ((.005, .19), (.01, .04)):
423        a = rng.binomial(100 * 100, .20, 400_000)
424        b = rng.binomial(100 * 100, .20 - gap, 400_000)
425        print(f'P(wrong) at gap {gap:.3f}: simulated {(b >= a).mean():.3f}, hand estimate {formula}')
426
427    # The fast normal posterior should behave like exact Beta Thompson Sampling.
428    P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd = make_worlds('factorial', 100)
429    n0, s0 = run_pilot('factorial', P0, batch_sd, 100)
430    fast = run_loop(dict(kind='ts'), P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, np.random.default_rng(3), 32_400)
431    exact = run_loop(dict(kind='ts_exact'), P0, P1, change_at, batch_sd, n0, s0, np.random.default_rng(4), 32_400)
432    diff = fast['regret'] - exact['regret']
433    print(f'TS regret over 30,000 pulls: normal {fast["regret"].mean():,.0f}, exact Beta '
434          f'{exact["regret"].mean():,.0f}, difference {diff.mean():,.0f} '
435          f'(SE {diff.std(ddof=1) / math.sqrt(len(diff)):,.0f})')
436
437
438if __name__ == '__main__':
439    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
440    parser.add_argument('command', choices=['bench', 'validate', 'run'])
441    parser.add_argument('--reps', type=int, default=200)
442    args = parser.parse_args()
443    if args.command == 'bench':
444        bench(args.reps)
445    elif args.command == 'validate':
446        validate()
447    else:
448        run_all(args.reps)
449    sys.exit(0)

 57class ProgressModel(UniformModel):
 58    """Uniform selection that prints each live result and running totals once it is saved."""
 59
 60    def __init__(self, target):
 61        super().__init__()
 62        self.target = target
 63        self.live = False
 64
 65    def fit(self, results):
 66        self.live = False  # Replaying saved history isn't new progress.
 67        super().fit(results)
 68        self.live = True
 69        return self
 70
 71    def update(self, result):
 72        super().update(result)
 73        if self.live:
 74            self.print_progress(result)
 75
 76    def fit_aggregates(self, rows):
 77        self.live = False
 78        super().fit_aggregates(rows)
 79        self.live = True
 80        return self
 81
 82    def print_progress(self, result):
 83        arm = int(result["Arm"])
 84        rates = {i: self.signups[i] / (VISITORS_PER_PULL * self.counts[i])
 85                 for i in range(ARMS) if self.counts[i]}
 86        high, low = max(rates, key=rates.get), min(rates, key=rates.get)
 87        total = sum(self.signups)
 88        print("Result:", result, flush=True)
 89        print("  Saved {}/{} ({:.1%}) | arm {}: {} sign-ups, {:.2%} over {} pulls | "
 90              "total {} ({:.2%}), server NetReward {} | highest arm {} {:.2%} | lowest arm {} {:.2%}".format(
 91                  self.total_pulls, self.target, self.total_pulls / self.target, arm, result["Reward"],
 92                  rates[arm], self.counts[arm], total, total / (VISITORS_PER_PULL * self.total_pulls),
 93                  result["NetReward"], high, rates[high], low, rates[low]), flush=True)

 96class ConsoleLog(OnlineLog):
 97    """The runner's event log, which also prints retries of an uncertain request."""
 98
 99    def __init__(self, path, run_id, seen):
100        super().__init__(path, run_id)
101        self.seen = seen
102        self.attempts = None
103
104    def write(self, event, **fields):
105        super().write(event, **fields)
106        attempt, arm = fields.get("attempt"), (fields.get("request") or {}).get("arm")
107        if event == "run_started":
108            self.attempts = fields["max_retries"] + 1 if fields['max_retries'] is not None else 'unlimited'
109        elif event == "pull_uncertain":
110            print("Arm {}: no reliable response on attempt {} of {} ({}). {}".format(
111                arm, attempt, self.attempts, uncertain_reason(self.seen["status"]),
112                "Retrying the same request." if fields["retry_scheduled"] else "No retries left."), flush=True)
113        elif event == "pull_completed" and attempt > 1:
114            print("Arm {}: response received on attempt {}. It was the same request, so it counts "
115                  "as one pull.".format(arm, attempt), flush=True)
116

118def uncertain_reason(status):
119    """Why a pull response couldn't be trusted, from the last HTTP status seen."""
120    if status is None:
121        return "timed out or the connection dropped"
122    if status == 429:
123        return "rate-limited, HTTP 429"
124    if status >= 500:
125        return "server error or still waking up, HTTP {}".format(status)
126    if status == 200:
127        return "the response wasn't valid"
128    return "HTTP {}".format(status)

131@contextmanager
132def windows_lock(path):
133    """Windows version of bandit.storage.driver_lock, which needs fcntl (macOS/Linux only)."""
134    import msvcrt
135
136    path = Path(path).expanduser().resolve()
137    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
138    with path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".lock").open("a+") as handle:
139        handle.seek(0)
140        try:
141            msvcrt.locking(handle.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_NBLCK, 1)
142        except OSError:
143            raise RuntimeError("Another driver is using this database") from None
144        try:
145            yield
146        finally:
147            handle.seek(0)
148            msvcrt.locking(handle.fileno(), msvcrt.LK_UNLCK, 1)
149

152    runner.driver_lock = windows_lock

183@contextmanager
184def record_http_status(seen):
185    """Note each HTTP status code, which server_pull hides from its callers. Nothing else is kept."""
186    original = server_pull._request
187
188    def request(*args, **kwargs):
189        seen["status"] = None
190        code, data = original(*args, **kwargs)
191        seen["status"] = code
192        return code, data
193
194    server_pull._request = request
195    try:
196        yield
197    finally:
198        server_pull._request = original
199

201@contextmanager
202def console_log(seen):
203    """Have the runner's event log also print retries to the console."""
204    original = runner.OnlineLog
205    runner.OnlineLog = partial(ConsoleLog, seen=seen)
206    try:
207        yield
208    finally:

212def describe_failure(error, status):
213    """Return what happened and what to do. Never echoes server text, which can be arbitrary."""
214    retry = "Run the same command again. Any unfinished request is retried safely."
215    if isinstance(error, ConfigError):
216        return str(error), "Fix config.py, then run again."
217    if status in HTTP_FAILURES:
218        return HTTP_FAILURES[status]
219    if status is not None and status >= 500:
220        return ("The server had a problem or is still waking up (HTTP {}).".format(status),
221                "Wait a few minutes. " + retry)
222    if isinstance(error, server_pull.UncertainPullError):
223        if status == 200:
224            return "The server replied, but its response wasn't valid.", "Contact the teaching team if this repeats."
225        return "No reliable response arrived, even after retries.", "Check your connection. " + retry
226    if isinstance(error, (ConnectionError, TimeoutError, http.client.HTTPException)):
227        return ("Couldn't get a response from the server. It may be waking up, or the connection dropped.",
228                "Check your connection and wait a minute. " + retry)
229    if isinstance(error, sqlite3.Error):
230        return ("Couldn't read or write the database ({}).".format(type(error).__name__),
231                "Close anything else using it and check the disk, then run again. Don't delete the database.")
232    if isinstance(error, OSError):
233        return "Couldn't use a local file: {}".format(error), "Check DB_PATH, LOG_PATH and the disk, then run again."
234    if isinstance(error, EOFError):
235        return "Couldn't read the username or password.", "Run this in PowerShell, cmd or Windows Terminal."
236    if isinstance(error, (RuntimeError, ValueError)):
237        # HTTP rejections were handled above, so these messages come from local code.
238        message = str(error)
239        if "Another driver" in message:
240            return message + ".", "Let the other run finish or close it, then run again."
241        if "belongs to another group" in message:
242            return message + ".", "Use the group account this database was started with."
243        return message + ".", "Check config.py. Contact the teaching team if this repeats."
244    return "Unexpected error ({}).".format(type(error).__name__), "Contact whoever maintains this script."

254    print("Saved so far: {} pulls.".format(len(results)), file=sys.stderr)
255    if pending:
256        print("Arm {} has an unfinished request. The next online run retries it first.".format(pending["arm"]),
257              file=sys.stderr)
258
259
260def saved_state(db_path):
261    with runner.driver_lock(db_path), HistoryStore(db_path) as store:
262        return list(store.results()), store.pending
263
264
265def rewards_by_arm(results):
266    by_arm = [[] for _ in range(ARMS)]
267    for row in results:
268        by_arm[int(row["Arm"])].append(row["Reward"])
269    return by_arm
270
271
272def remaining_pulls(by_arm):
273    return sum(max(0, config.PULLS_PER_ARM - len(rewards)) for rewards in by_arm)
274
275
276def server_matches_history(username, password, local_pulls, pending):
277    """Compare the account with saved history before any pull. Status uses no budget."""
278    with PacedClient(username, password, SERVER_URL, interval=config.REQUEST_INTERVAL,
279                     timeout=config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT) as client:
280        used = integer(client.status().get("PullsUsed"), "server PullsUsed", maximum=MAX_PULLS)
281    print("Server pulls used: {}. Saved locally: {}.".format(used, local_pulls))
282    # A pending request may already be recorded on the server but not yet saved here.
283    if used < local_pulls:
284        print("Stopped: saved history is ahead of the server. Check the group and database.")
285        return False
286    if used > local_pulls + bool(pending) and not config.ALLOW_UNSAVED_SERVER_PULLS:
287        print("Stopped: the server has pulls this database does not. Find out who made them "
288              "and import any saved responses. No pulls were made.")
289        return False
290    return True
291
292
293def noise_ratio(by_arm):
294    """Observed batch variance over the binomial variance; about 1 if batches are binomial."""
295    observed, expected, df = 0.0, 0.0, 0
296    for rewards in by_arm:
297        if len(rewards) >= 2:
298            rate = mean(rewards) / VISITORS_PER_PULL
299            observed += (len(rewards) - 1) * variance(rewards)
300            expected += (len(rewards) - 1) * VISITORS_PER_PULL * rate * (1 - rate)
301            df += len(rewards) - 1
302    return (observed / expected, df) if expected else (None, 0)
303
304
305def stability(by_arm):
306    """Standardized change from each arm's first half of pulls to its last half."""
307    scores, shift, spread = [], 0.0, 0.0
308    for rewards in by_arm:
309        half = len(rewards) // 2
310        rate = mean(rewards) / VISITORS_PER_PULL if rewards else 0
311        if half >= 2 and 0 < rate < 1:
312            change = mean(rewards[-half:]) - mean(rewards[:half])
313            error = 2 * VISITORS_PER_PULL * rate * (1 - rate) / half
314            scores.append(change / math.sqrt(error))
315            shift += change
316            spread += error
317    return scores, (shift / math.sqrt(spread) if spread else None)
318
319
320def report(by_arm, completed, elapsed):
321    print("\n{:>3} {:>6} {:>9} {:>10}".format("Arm", "Pulls", "Sign-ups", "Rate"))
322    for arm, rewards in enumerate(by_arm):
323        rate = "{:.2%}".format(mean(rewards) / VISITORS_PER_PULL) if rewards else "-"
324        print("{:>3} {:>6} {:>9} {:>10}".format(arm, len(rewards), sum(rewards), rate))
325
326    pulls = sum(len(rewards) for rewards in by_arm)
327    print("\nTotal saved: {} pulls, {} sign-ups. {} pulls left in this phase.".format(
328        pulls, sum(sum(rewards) for rewards in by_arm), remaining_pulls(by_arm)))
329    if completed and elapsed > 0:
330        speed = completed / elapsed
331        print("Speed: {:.2f} pulls per second. The rest of the budget would take {:.0f} hours.".format(
332            speed, (MAX_PULLS - pulls) / speed / 3600))
333
334    ratio, df = noise_ratio(by_arm)
335    scores, overall = stability(by_arm)
336    if ratio is None or not scores:
337        print("Noise and stability checks need at least 4 pulls per arm.")
338        return
339    print("Noise: variance is {:.2f} times binomial (about 1 +/- {:.2f} is normal).".format(
340        ratio, 2 * math.sqrt(2 / df)))
341    print("Stability: {} of {} arms moved by more than 2 standard errors (0 to 3 is normal). "
342          "Largest move: {:.1f}. All arms together: {:.1f}.".format(
343              sum(abs(score) > 2 for score in scores), len(scores),
344              max(abs(score) for score in scores), overall))
345
346
347def main():
348    password, db_path = None, None
349    seen = {"status": None}
350    try:
351        validate_config()
352        db_path = resolve_path(config.DB_PATH)
353        log_path = resolve_path(config.LOG_PATH) if config.LOG_PATH is not None else None
354        results, pending = saved_state(db_path)
355        by_arm = rewards_by_arm(results)
356        # Uniform always picks the least-pulled arm, so these pulls only fill arms below target.
357        budget = min(config.MAX_PULLS_THIS_RUN, remaining_pulls(by_arm)) if config.ONLINE else 0
358        print("Mode: {}. Pulls planned this run: {}.".format("ONLINE" if config.ONLINE else "OFFLINE", budget))
359
360        completed, elapsed, stop_reason = 0, 0.0, None
361        if budget > 0:
362            username = config.GROUP_USERNAME.strip() or input("Group username: ").strip()
363            if not username:
364                raise ConfigError("A group username is required. Enter one or set GROUP_USERNAME.")
365            password = os.environ.get("GP3_PASSWORD") or getpass("Group password: ")
366            with record_http_status(seen), console_log(seen):
367                if not server_matches_history(username, password, len(results), pending):
368                    return 1
369                if pending:
370                    print("Arm {} has an unfinished request from an earlier run. Retrying it first; "
371                          "it counts as one of this run's pulls.".format(pending["arm"]))
372                started = time.monotonic()
373                model = ProgressModel(len(results) + remaining_pulls(by_arm))
374                summary = run_experiment(model, budget, online=True, db_path=db_path,
375                                         username=username, password=password, server_url=SERVER_URL,
376                                         interval=config.REQUEST_INTERVAL, timeout=config.REQUEST_TIMEOUT,
377                                         max_retries=config.MAX_RETRIES, log_path=log_path)
378            completed, elapsed = summary["completed_pulls"], time.monotonic() - started
379            stop_reason = summary["stop_reason"]
380            print("Completed {} pulls. Stop reason: {}.".format(completed, stop_reason))
381            results, pending = saved_state(db_path)
382
383        if stop_reason in STOP_MESSAGES:
384            print("Run stopped: {}".format(STOP_MESSAGES[stop_reason]), file=sys.stderr)
385        if pending:
386            print("A request is still pending for arm {}. Rerun online to recover it.".format(pending["arm"]))
387        report(rewards_by_arm(results), completed, elapsed)
388        print("\nDatabase:", db_path)
389        return 1 if stop_reason in STOP_MESSAGES else 0
390    except KeyboardInterrupt:
391        print("Interrupted. Run the same command again to continue.", file=sys.stderr)
392        print_saved_state(db_path)
393        return 130
394    except Exception as error:
395        what, action = describe_failure(error, seen["status"])
396        print("Run stopped: {}\nWhat to do: {}".format(what, action), file=sys.stderr)
397        print_saved_state(db_path)
398        return 1
399    finally:
400        password = None
401
402
403if __name__ == "__main__":
404    raise SystemExit(main())
