 59def draw_worlds(counts, signups, worlds, seed):
 60    """Defensive importance sampling, q=.5*posterior+.5*challenger mixtures.
 61
 62    Only a challenger's rate is tilted. Evaluate the complete mixture density,
 63    not just the sampled component; posterior/q weights are bounded above by 2.
 64    This samples rare wrong-leader situations without giving them artificial mass.
 65    """
 66    import numpy as np
 67    a, b = 1 + np.asarray(signups), 1 + 100*np.asarray(counts)-np.asarray(signups)
 68    mean = a / (a+b)
 69    leader = int(mean.argmax())
 70    challengers = np.array([i for i in range(ARMS) if i != leader])
 71    concentration = np.minimum(a+b, 20000.)
 72    target = np.minimum(.9999, mean[leader] + .5*np.sqrt(mean*(1-mean)/(a+b+1)))
 73    qa, qb = target*concentration, (1-target)*concentration
 74    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
 75    p = rng.beta(a, b, size=(worlds, ARMS))
 76    component = rng.integers(0, len(challengers), size=worlds)
 77    tilted = rng.random(worlds) < .5
 78    lanes = np.flatnonzero(tilted)
 79    chosen = challengers[component[lanes]]
 80    p[lanes, chosen] = rng.beta(qa[chosen], qb[chosen])
 81    def lbeta(x, y):
 82        return np.array([math.lgamma(float(v))+math.lgamma(float(w))-math.lgamma(float(v+w))
 83                         for v, w in zip(x, y)])
 84    clipped = np.clip(p[:, challengers], np.finfo(float).tiny, 1-np.finfo(float).eps)
 85    ratios = ((qa-a)[challengers]*np.log(clipped) +
 86              (qb-b)[challengers]*np.log1p(-clipped) +
 87              (lbeta(a, b)-lbeta(qa, qb))[challengers])
 88    # log-sum-exp including the .5 posterior component prevents overflow.
 89    log_terms = np.concatenate((np.full((worlds, 1), math.log(.5)),
 90                                ratios + math.log(.5/len(challengers))), axis=1)
 91    maximum = log_terms.max(axis=1)
 92    log_q_over_p = maximum + np.log(np.exp(log_terms-maximum[:, None]).sum(axis=1))
 93    weights = np.exp(-log_q_over_p)
 94    return p, weights
 95
 96
 97def rollout(worlds, counts, signups, candidates, baseline, stage, horizon, seed, trace=False):
 98    """Exact sequential UCB decisions; O(candidates*worlds*arms) working memory.
 99
100    After `stage`, every lane uses baseline as a *learning* continuation policy.
101    The policy sees simulated observations, never latent rates. Arrays of full
102    response histories are not retained. trace is restricted to a single test lane.
103    """
104    import numpy as np
105    copies, reps = len(candidates), len(worlds)
106    p = np.tile(worlds, (copies, 1))
107    n = np.tile(np.asarray(counts, dtype=float), (copies*reps, 1))
108    s = np.tile(np.asarray(signups, dtype=float), (copies*reps, 1))
109    lanes = np.arange(len(p))
110    coefficients = np.repeat([round(2*c*c, 12) for c in candidates], reps)[:, None]
111    baseline_coefficient = round(2*baseline*baseline, 12)
112    mean = np.divide(s, 100*n, out=np.zeros_like(s), where=n > 0)
113    inverse = np.divide(1., np.sqrt(n), out=np.full_like(n, np.inf), where=n > 0)
114    losses = np.zeros(len(p))
115    short = np.zeros(len(p))
116    best = p.max(axis=1)
117    start = int(sum(counts))
118    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
119    history = [] if trace else None
120    if trace and (len(p) != 1 or horizon > 10000):
121        raise ValueError('Trace is for small single-lane tests only')
122    for step in range(horizon):
123        if step == stage:
124            coefficients.fill(baseline_coefficient)
125        # log(max(t,2)) handles empty histories while unseen arms remain +inf.
126        scores = mean + np.sqrt(coefficients * math.log(max(start+step, 2))) * inverse
127        arms = scores.argmax(axis=1)
128        probabilities = p[lanes, arms]
129        reward = rng.binomial(100, probabilities)
130        losses += 100*(best-probabilities)
131        n[lanes, arms] += 1
132        s[lanes, arms] += reward
133        mean[lanes, arms] = s[lanes, arms]/(100*n[lanes, arms])
134        inverse[lanes, arms] = 1/np.sqrt(n[lanes, arms])
135        if step+1 == stage:
136            short[:] = losses
137        if trace:
138            history.append((int(arms[0]), int(reward[0])))
139    return {'full': losses.reshape(copies, reps), 'stage': short.reshape(copies, reps),
140            'trace': history}
141
142
143def weighted_cvar(loss, weights, level):
144    """Upper-tail empirical CVaR, equivalent to min_eta eta+E[(L-eta)+]/(1-alpha).
145
146    At an atom spanning the quantile, include only the mass needed to complete
147    the tail. Averaging all losses >= VaR would be incorrect for discrete data.
148    """
149    import numpy as np
150    loss, weights = np.asarray(loss, dtype=float), np.asarray(weights, dtype=float)
151    if (loss.ndim != 1 or weights.shape != loss.shape or not len(loss)
152            or not np.isfinite(loss).all() or not np.isfinite(weights).all()
153            or (weights < 0).any() or not weights.max() > 0
154            or not math.isfinite(level) or not 0 <= level < 1):
155        raise ValueError('CVaR requires finite losses, nonnegative mass and 0 <= level < 1')
156    weights = weights/weights.max()
157    order = np.argsort(-loss)
158    w = weights[order]/weights.sum()
159    mass = 1-level
160    used = np.minimum(w, np.maximum(0., mass-(np.cumsum(w)-w)))
161    return float(np.sum(used*loss[order])/mass)
162
163
164def _mean_error(values, weights):
165    import numpy as np
166    w = weights/weights.sum()
167    mean = float(np.sum(w*values))
168    ess = float(1/np.sum(w*w))
169    error = float(np.sqrt(np.sum(w*w*(values-mean)**2)*ess/max(ess-1, 1)))
170    return mean, error, ess
171
172
173def _tail_ess(loss, weights, level):
174    import numpy as np
175    order = np.argsort(-loss)
176    mass = weights[order]/weights.sum()
177    used = np.minimum(mass, np.maximum(0., 1-level-(np.cumsum(mass)-mass)))
178    return float(used.sum()**2/np.sum(used**2))
179
180
181def validate_switch(candidate, baseline, weights, config):
182    """Conservative Monte Carlo screening, NOT a distribution-free guarantee."""
183    import numpy as np
184    full, full_se, ess = _mean_error(candidate['full']-baseline['full'], weights)
185    short, short_se, _ = _mean_error(candidate['stage']-baseline['stage'], weights)
186    tail = weighted_cvar(candidate['full'], weights, config.cvar_level) - weighted_cvar(
187        baseline['full'], weights, config.cvar_level)
188    # Paired bootstrap of proposal draws; retain importance weights in each sample.
189    rng = np.random.default_rng(config.seed+12345)
190    differences = []
191    for _ in range(96):
192        ix = rng.integers(0, len(weights), len(weights))
193        if weights[ix].sum() <= 0:
194            return {'accepted': False, 'reason': 'insufficient_importance_mass'}
195        differences.append(weighted_cvar(candidate['full'][ix], weights[ix], config.cvar_level) -
196                           weighted_cvar(baseline['full'][ix], weights[ix], config.cvar_level))
197    tail_se = float(np.std(differences, ddof=1))
198    # At least a few effective tail draws; otherwise never claim tail safety.
199    tail_ess = min(_tail_ess(candidate['full'], weights, config.cvar_level),
200                   _tail_ess(baseline['full'], weights, config.cvar_level))
201    enough = ess >= config.min_ess and tail_ess >= 4
202    full_upper, short_upper, tail_upper = full+2.58*full_se, short+2.58*short_se, tail+2.58*tail_se
203    accepted = (enough and full_upper < -config.min_gain and
204                short_upper <= config.stage_loss_allowance and tail_upper <= config.tail_loss_allowance)
205    return {'accepted': bool(accepted), 'ess': ess, 'tail_ess': tail_ess, 'full_regret_difference': full,
206            'stage_regret_difference': short, 'cvar_difference': tail,
207            'full_difference_upper': full_upper, 'stage_difference_upper': short_upper,
208            'cvar_difference_upper': tail_upper, 'reason': 'validated' if accepted else 'safeguard_or_uncertainty'}
209
210
211def evaluate(stats, remaining, baseline, config):
212    import numpy as np
213    integer(remaining, 'remaining', maximum=MAX_PULLS)
214    from .models import UCBModel
215    model = UCBModel(round(2*baseline**2, 12)).fit_aggregates(stats)
216    n, s = np.array(model.counts), np.array(model.signups)
217    candidates = sorted(set((*config.candidates, baseline)))
218    stage = min(config.interval, remaining)
219    result = {'selected_multiplier': baseline, 'baseline_multiplier': baseline,
220              'horizon': remaining, 'stage_horizon': stage, 'reason': 'baseline_retained',
221              'continuation': 'current_multiplier_with_sequential_learning', 'candidates': []}
222    if not remaining or not np.all(n > 0):
223        result['reason'] = 'no_budget_or_unseen_arms'
224        return result
225    seed = config.seed + int(n.sum())
226    p, w = draw_worlds(n, s, config.train_worlds, seed)
227    sample = rollout(p, n, s, candidates, baseline, stage, remaining, seed+1)
228    leader = int((s/(100*n)).argmax())
229    wrong = p.argmax(axis=1) != leader
230    wrong_mass = float(w[wrong].sum()/w.sum())
231    for j, c in enumerate(candidates):
232        full, error, ess = _mean_error(sample['full'][j], w)
233        short = float(np.average(sample['stage'][j], weights=w))
234        result['candidates'].append({
235            'multiplier': c, 'expected_full_regret': full, 'expected_stage_regret': short,
236            'expected_full_signups': float(100*remaining*np.average(p.max(axis=1), weights=w)-full),
237            'expected_stage_signups': float(100*stage*np.average(p.max(axis=1), weights=w)-short),
238            'full_regret_mc_se': error, 'ess': ess,
239            'cvar': weighted_cvar(sample['full'][j], w, config.cvar_level),
240            'leader_wrong_probability': wrong_mass,
241            'regret_if_leader_wrong': float(np.average(sample['full'][j, wrong], weights=w[wrong]))
242                if w[wrong].sum() else None})
243    base = next(row for row in result['candidates'] if row['multiplier'] == baseline)
244    feasible = [row for row in result['candidates']
245                if row['expected_stage_regret'] <= base['expected_stage_regret']+config.stage_loss_allowance
246                and row['cvar'] <= base['cvar']+config.tail_loss_allowance]
247    chosen = min(feasible, key=lambda row: (row['expected_full_regret'], row['multiplier'] != baseline))
248    if chosen['multiplier'] == baseline:
249        return result
250    # Independent worlds AND independent observation noise, for one preselected challenger.
251    vp, vw = draw_worlds(n, s, config.validation_worlds, seed+1000003)
252    validation = rollout(vp, n, s, [chosen['multiplier'], baseline], baseline,
253                         stage, remaining, seed+1000004)
254    gate = validate_switch({k: validation[k][0] for k in ('full', 'stage')},
255                           {k: validation[k][1] for k in ('full', 'stage')}, vw, config)
256    result['validation'] = gate
257    result['proposed_multiplier'] = chosen['multiplier']
258    result['reason'] = gate['reason']
259    if gate['accepted']:
260        result['selected_multiplier'] = chosen['multiplier']
261    return result
262
263
264def evaluate_isolated(stats, remaining, baseline, config, stop=None):
265    """Worker has no credentials, network code or history database connection."""
266    fallback = {'selected_multiplier': baseline, 'baseline_multiplier': baseline,
267                'horizon': remaining, 'stage_horizon': min(config.interval, remaining)}
268    if stop:
269        stop.check()
270    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='gp3-tune-') as folder:
271        request, output = Path(folder)/'input.json', Path(folder)/'output.json'
272        request.write_text(json.dumps({'stats': stats, 'remaining': remaining,
273                                      'baseline': baseline, 'config': asdict(config)}))
274        # Allowlist rather than copying authentication/environment from the driver.
275        env = {key: os.environ[key] for key in ('PATH', 'SYSTEMROOT', 'TMPDIR', 'LANG') if key in os.environ}
276        env.update(OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS='1', OMP_NUM_THREADS='1', MKL_NUM_THREADS='1',
277                   PYTHONNOUSERSITE='1')
278        proc = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-m', 'bandit.tuning_worker', str(request), str(output)],
279                                cwd=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1], env=env,
280                                stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
281                                stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
282        started = time.monotonic()
283        try:
284            while proc.poll() is None:
285                if stop:
286                    stop.check()
287                if time.monotonic()-started >= config.max_seconds:
288                    return {**fallback, 'reason': 'timeout'}
289                if stop:
290                    stop.wait(.1)
291                else:
292                    time.sleep(.1)
293            if stop:
294                stop.check()
295            if proc.returncode != 0 or not output.is_file() or output.stat().st_size > 1_000_000:
296                return {**fallback, 'reason': 'worker_failed'}
297            try:
298                result = json.loads(output.read_text())
299                if result['selected_multiplier'] not in (*config.candidates, baseline):
300                    raise ValueError('Invalid worker selection')
301                return result
302            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
303                return {**fallback, 'reason': 'invalid_worker_result'}
304        finally:
305            if proc.poll() is None:
306                proc.terminate()
307                try:
308                    proc.wait(timeout=2)
309                except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
310                    proc.kill()
311                    proc.wait()
312            else:
313                proc.wait()

14def integer(value, name, minimum=0, maximum=None):
15    if type(value) is not int or value < minimum or (maximum is not None and value > maximum):
16        raise ValueError("Invalid {}".format(name))
17    return value
18

20def server_address(value):
21    if not isinstance(value, str):
22        raise ValueError("Server must be an HTTPS base address")
23    parts = urlsplit(value)
24    if (parts.scheme != "https" or not parts.netloc or parts.username or parts.password
25            or parts.query or parts.fragment or parts.path not in ("", "/")):
26        raise ValueError("Server must be an HTTPS base address without credentials or path")
27    return value.rstrip("/")

30def normalize_result(value):
31    """Copy only the four documented fields; reject invalid observations."""
32    if not isinstance(value, dict) or not {"Arm", "Reward", "NetReward", "Pull"} <= value.keys():
33        raise ValueError("A result must contain Arm, Reward, NetReward and Pull")
34    arm = value["Arm"]
35    if isinstance(arm, str) and arm in {str(i) for i in range(ARMS)}:
36        arm = int(arm)
37    integer(arm, "arm", maximum=ARMS - 1)
38    reward = integer(value["Reward"], "reward", maximum=VISITORS_PER_PULL)
39    pull = integer(value["Pull"], "pull", maximum=MAX_PULLS - 1)
40    total = integer(value["NetReward"], "net reward", minimum=reward,
41                    maximum=(pull + 1) * VISITORS_PER_PULL)
42    return {"Arm": str(arm), "Reward": reward, "NetReward": total, "Pull": pull}

report/build_report.pyBuilds this HTML file from our saved results · 1,477 lines
   1#!/usr/bin/env python3
   2"""Build GP3_group19_analysis.html: the code, results and LLM prompts behind our bandit run.
   3
   4Read-only and offline:
   5  - copies one consistent snapshot of the shared database with SQLite's backup API, which
   6    holds a read lock for well under a second (inside the live driver's 5-second busy
   7    timeout), then analyses only that copy;
   8  - streams the event log read-only;
   9  - makes no HTTP requests, never imports server_pull and never asks for the password.
  10
  11Rebuild using the full database, event log and pre-pilot outputs (see the input note at the end):
  12
  13    python report/build_report.py
  14
  15Needs numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib and pygments.

 118# ---------------------------------------------------------------- source excerpts
 119def _find(tree, parts):
 120    body, node = tree.body, None
 121    for depth, part in enumerate(parts):
 122        for candidate in body:
 123            if isinstance(candidate, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)) and candidate.name == part:
 124                node = candidate
 125                break
 126            if depth == len(parts) - 1 and isinstance(candidate, (ast.Assign, ast.AnnAssign)):
 127                targets = candidate.targets if isinstance(candidate, ast.Assign) else [candidate.target]
 128                if any(isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == part for t in targets):
 129                    node = candidate
 130                    break
 131        else:
 132            raise KeyError(".".join(parts))
 133        body = getattr(node, "body", [])
 134    return node

 137def excerpt(rel, name=None):
 138    """Exact source of one function, class, method ("Class.method") or assignment in a project file.
 139
 140    `rel` is relative to the repository. Line numbers are the file's own, so the page can be
 141    checked against the repository.
 142    """
 143    path = (REPO / rel).resolve()
 144    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
 145    lines = text.splitlines()
 146    shown = rel[3:] + " (beside the repo)" if rel.startswith("../") else rel
 147    if name is None:
 148        return {"rel": rel, "shown": shown, "name": None, "start": 1, "end": len(lines), "code": text.rstrip("\n")}
 149    node = _find(ast.parse(text), name.split("."))
 150    start = min([node.lineno] + [d.lineno for d in getattr(node, "decorator_list", [])])
 151    code = textwrap.dedent("\n".join(lines[start - 1:node.end_lineno]))
 152    return {"rel": rel, "shown": shown, "name": name, "start": start, "end": node.end_lineno, "code": code}

 155def use_function(rel, name, **namespace):
 156    """Run the exact function shown on the page, so the code and its output can't drift apart."""
 157    block = excerpt(rel, name)
 158    exec(compile(block["code"], "{}:{}".format(rel, name), "exec"), namespace)
 159    return namespace[name]

 163def snapshot(target):
 164    """Copy one consistent snapshot of the live database. The source is opened read-only."""
 165    source = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH.as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True, timeout=2)
 166    copy = sqlite3.connect(str(target))
 167    try:
 168        source.backup(copy)
 169    finally:
 170        source.close()
 171        copy.close()

 174def load_data(db):
 175    """Every saved pull, the pending request (if any) and the tuning decisions, from the snapshot."""
 176    con = sqlite3.connect(str(db))
 177    try:
 178        df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT pull, arm, reward, net_reward, saved_at, model, parameters, request_id "
 179                               "FROM results ORDER BY pull", con)
 180        pending = con.execute("SELECT payload FROM pending WHERE singleton = 1").fetchone()
 181        try:
 182            tuning = [json.loads(p) for (p,) in con.execute("SELECT payload FROM tuning_decisions ORDER BY id")]
 183        except sqlite3.OperationalError:
 184            tuning = []
 185    finally:
 186        con.close()
 187    df["time"] = pd.to_datetime(df["saved_at"], format="ISO8601", utc=True)
 188    parsed = {p: json.loads(p).get("exploration", np.nan) for p in df["parameters"].unique()}
 189    df["exploration"] = df["parameters"].map(parsed).astype(float)
 190    return df, (json.loads(pending[0]) if pending else None), tuning

 193def live_runs(log_path):
 194    """Start and end of every live run, from the append-only event log (streamed, read-only)."""
 195    if not log_path.is_file():
 196        return []
 197    runs, order = {}, []
 198    with open(log_path, "rb") as handle:
 199        for line in handle:
 200            if not (b'"run_started"' in line or b'"run_finished"' in line or b'"run_failed"' in line):
 201                continue
 202            try:
 203                event = json.loads(line)
 204            except ValueError:
 205                continue  # A partly written final line
 206            kind, run_id = event.get("event"), event.get("run_id")
 207            if kind == "run_started":
 208                runs[run_id] = {"start": event, "end": None}
 209                order.append(run_id)
 210            elif kind in ("run_finished", "run_failed") and run_id in runs:
 211                runs[run_id]["end"] = event
 212    return [runs[r] for r in order]

 215# ---------------------------------------------------------------- analysis
 216def prob_best(a, b, draws=400_000, seed=SEED):
 217    """Share of joint Beta posterior draws in which each arm has the highest rate."""
 218    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
 219    wins = np.zeros(len(a))
 220    for done in range(0, draws, 50_000):
 221        size = min(50_000, draws - done)
 222        wins += np.bincount(rng.beta(a, b, size=(size, len(a))).argmax(axis=1), minlength=len(a))
 223    return wins / draws
 224
 225
 226def arm_summary(part, draws=400_000):
 227    """Pulls, sign-ups, rate, Beta(1 + sign-ups, 1 + non-sign-ups) 95% interval and P(best) per arm."""
 228    g = part.groupby("arm")["reward"].agg(pulls="size", signups="sum").reindex(range(K), fill_value=0)
 229    a, b = 1 + g["signups"], 1 + V * g["pulls"] - g["signups"]
 230    g["rate"] = g["signups"] / (V * g["pulls"])
 231    g["low"], g["high"] = stats.beta.ppf(0.025, a, b), stats.beta.ppf(0.975, a, b)
 232    g["p_best"] = prob_best(a.to_numpy(float), b.to_numpy(float), draws)
 233    return g

 236def leader_of(summary):
 237    """The arm whose 95% interval has the highest lower end."""

 243    n = len(df)

 246         bool((df["pull"].to_numpy() == np.arange(n)).all())),
 247        ("Every NetReward equals the running total of Reward",
 248         bool((df["net_reward"] == df["reward"].cumsum()).all())),
 249        ("Every arm is 0 to 23 and every Reward is 0 to 100",
 250         bool(df["arm"].between(0, K - 1).all() and df["reward"].between(0, V).all())),
 251        ("Every request ID is unique", bool(df["request_id"].dropna().is_unique)),
 252    ]

 255def replay_ucb(df):
 256    """Re-make every saved UCB choice from the pulls before it, with UCBModel's score and tie-break.
 257
 258    Score = mean + sqrt(exploration * ln(total pulls) / arm pulls). The highest score wins and
 259    ties go to the lowest arm, as in program/bandit/models.py. Each pull uses its saved exploration.
 260    """
 261    arms, rewards = df["arm"].to_numpy(), df["reward"].to_numpy()
 262    exploration, is_ucb = df["exploration"].to_numpy(), (df["model"] == "ucb").to_numpy()
 263    counts, signups, means = [0] * K, [0] * K, [0.0] * K
 264    checked = mismatched = 0
 265    first = None
 266    for i in range(len(arms)):
 267        if is_ucb[i]:
 268            scale = float(exploration[i]) * math.log(i)  # i pulls were saved before this one
 269            best, best_score = 0, -math.inf
 270            for arm in range(K):
 271                c = counts[arm]
 272                score = math.inf if c == 0 else means[arm] + math.sqrt(scale / c)
 273                if score > best_score:
 274                    best, best_score = arm, score
 275            checked += 1
 276            if best != arms[i]:
 277                mismatched += 1
 278                first = i if first is None else first
 279        arm = int(arms[i])
 280        counts[arm] += 1
 281        signups[arm] += int(rewards[i])
 282        means[arm] = signups[arm] / (V * counts[arm])
 283    return {"checked": checked, "mismatched": mismatched, "first_mismatch": first}
 284

 286def checkpoint_view(df, cuts, leader):
 287    """At each checkpoint: the leader's and runner-up's rates and the leader's P(best)."""
 288    rows = []
 289    for cut in cuts:
 290        g = arm_summary(df.iloc[:cut], draws=200_000)
 291        others = g.drop(index=leader).sort_values("rate", ascending=False)
 292        runner = int(others.index[0])
 293        rows.append({"cut": cut, "leader_rate": g.at[leader, "rate"], "leader_pulls": int(g.at[leader, "pulls"]),
 294                     "runner": runner, "runner_rate": g.at[runner, "rate"], "runner_pulls": int(g.at[runner, "pulls"]),
 295                     "p_best": g.at[leader, "p_best"]})
 296    return rows

 299def stage_table(df, tuning, leader, final):
 300    """Pulls, sign-ups, conversion, share on the leader and speed for each stage of the live run.
 301
 302    Speed counts only gaps under 60 seconds between saved pulls, so pauses between runs and
 303    tuning checks don't count as running time.
 304    """
 305    n = len(df)
 306    starts = [d["at_pull"] for d in tuning] or [16_055]
 307    blocks = [(0, PILOT_PULLS, "Pilot"),
 308              (PILOT_PULLS, CHECKPOINTS[0], "Stage 1"),
 309              (CHECKPOINTS[0], starts[0], "Stage 2")]
 310    for i, start in enumerate(starts):
 311        end = starts[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(starts) else n
 312        label = "Stage 3.{}, after check {}".format(i + 1, i + 1)
 313        blocks.append((start, end, label + (" (running)" if end == n and not final else "")))
 314    by_arm = df.groupby("arm")["reward"]
 315    rate = by_arm.sum() / (V * by_arm.size())
 316    cost = V * (rate[leader] - rate.reindex(df["arm"]).to_numpy())  # Per pull, at the latest estimates
 317    rows = []
 318    for start, end, label in blocks:
 319        part = df.iloc[start:min(end, n)]
 320        if part.empty:
 321            continue
 322        gaps = part["time"].diff().dt.total_seconds().iloc[1:]
 323        running = gaps[gaps < 60]
 324        rows.append({"label": label, "first": start, "last": start + len(part) - 1, "pulls": len(part),
 325                     "signups": int(part["reward"].sum()), "on_leader": float((part["arm"] == leader).mean()),
 326                     "arms": int(part["arm"].nunique()), "method": method_label(part),
 327                     "speed": len(running) / running.sum() if running.sum() else float("nan"),
 328                     "cost": float(cost[start:start + len(part)].sum()),
 329                     "start": part["time"].iloc[0], "end": part["time"].iloc[-1]})
 330    return rows

 333def allocation_bins(df, leader, runners, bins=28):
 334    """Share of pulls on each arm in log-spaced windows of the pull number, after the pilot."""
 335    arms = df["arm"].to_numpy()
 336    edges = np.unique(np.geomspace(PILOT_PULLS, len(df), bins + 1).astype(int))
 337    rows = []
 338    for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
 339        window = arms[lo:hi]
 340        row = {"lo": lo, "hi": hi, "mid": math.sqrt(lo * hi), "others": float((window != leader).mean())}
 341        row.update({"arm{}".format(a): float((window == a).mean()) for a in runners})
 342        rows.append(row)
 343    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
 344
 345
 346def conversion_bins(df, bins=32):
 347    """Conversion rate in windows of the pull number, and the cumulative rate so far.
 348
 349    The pilot is one window; after it, windows are log-spaced.
 350    """
 351    rewards = df["reward"].to_numpy()
 352    total = np.cumsum(rewards)
 353    edges = np.unique(np.concatenate([[0], np.geomspace(PILOT_PULLS, len(df), bins).astype(int)]))
 354    rows = [{"lo": lo, "hi": hi, "mid": math.sqrt(max(lo, 1) * hi),
 355             "window": rewards[lo:hi].sum() / (V * (hi - lo)), "cumulative": total[hi - 1] / (V * hi)}
 356            for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:])]
 357    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
 358

 360def leader_stability(df, leader, blocks=20):
 361    """Has the leader's rate drifted? Its rate in 20 equal windows of the pull number, plus two tests.
 362
 363    With the full budget each window is 50,000 pulls. Chi-square: are the windows' sign-up rates
 364    consistent with one fixed rate? Dispersion: batch variance over the binomial variance
 365    100 p (1 - p); about 1 if batches are binomial.
 366    """
 367    rows = df[df["arm"] == leader]
 368    rewards, pulls = rows["reward"].to_numpy(), rows["pull"].to_numpy()
 369    edges = np.linspace(0, len(df), blocks + 1).astype(int)
 370    out = []
 371    for lo, hi in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
 372        inside = (pulls >= lo) & (pulls < hi)
 373        s, n = int(rewards[inside].sum()), int(inside.sum())
 374        if n == 0:
 375            continue
 376        rate = s / (V * n)
 377        half = 1.96 * math.sqrt(rate * (1 - rate) / (V * n))
 378        out.append({"first": int(lo), "last": int(hi) - 1, "pulls": n, "signups": s,
 379                    "rate": rate, "low": rate - half, "high": rate + half})
 380    out = pd.DataFrame(out)
 381    chi2, p_value, dof, _ = stats.chi2_contingency(np.column_stack([out["signups"], V * out["pulls"] - out["signups"]]))
 382    p = rewards.sum() / (V * len(rewards))
 383    dispersion = rewards.var(ddof=1) / (V * p * (1 - p))
 384    return out, {"chi2": chi2, "dof": dof, "p_value": p_value, "dispersion": dispersion,
 385                 "tolerance": 2 * math.sqrt(2 / (len(rewards) - 1)), "rate": p}
 386
 387
 388def projection(df):
 389    """Time to finish, and total sign-ups, if the rest of the budget runs like recent pulls.
 390
 391    Speed: the last 5,000 pulls (gaps over 60 s excluded). Rate: the last 100,000 pulls.
 392    The +/- range is binomial noise only (1.96 standard deviations).
 393    """
 394    remaining = MAX_PULLS - len(df)
 395    gaps = df["time"].iloc[-5_001:].diff().dt.total_seconds().iloc[1:]
 396    gaps = gaps[gaps < 60]
 397    speed = len(gaps) / gaps.sum()
 398    recent = df["reward"].iloc[-100_000:]
 399    rate = recent.sum() / (V * len(recent))
 400    finish = df["time"].iloc[-1] + timedelta(seconds=remaining / speed)
 401    return {"remaining": remaining, "speed": speed, "rate": rate, "finish": finish,
 402            "total": int(df["reward"].sum()) + V * remaining * rate,
 403            "noise": 1.96 * math.sqrt(V * remaining * rate * (1 - rate))}

 431    return "{:g}".format(value)

 454def chart_phase2(summary, worst, chosen):
 455    names = {"UCB": "UCB ×{:g}", "Thompson": "Thompson Sampling", "e-greedy": "ε-greedy, ε = {:g}"}
 456    colors = {"UCB": BLUE, "Thompson": ORANGE, "e-greedy": AQUA}

 467        ax.scatter(r.regret, y, s=44, color=c, edgecolors=SURFACE, linewidths=1.5, zorder=4)

 475    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
 476    ax.spines["left"].set_visible(False)
 477    ax.set_xscale("log")
 478    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(compact))
 479    ax.set_xlabel("Sign-ups lost against always pulling each world's best arm (log scale)")
 480    handles = [Line2D([], [], color=colors[m], marker="o", lw=0, markersize=7, label=label)
 481               for m, label in (("UCB", "UCB"), ("Thompson", "Thompson Sampling"), ("e-greedy", "ε-greedy"))]
 482    handles += [Line2D([], [], color=INK2, marker="o", lw=0, markersize=6, label="Mean of 200 worlds"),
 483                Line2D([], [], color=INK2, marker="|", lw=0, markersize=11, markeredgewidth=2, label="Worst world")]
 484    ax.legend(handles=handles, loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.45, -0.13), ncol=5, fontsize=8.5,
 485              handletextpad=0.3, columnspacing=1.4)
 486    return to_svg(fig, "Simulated sign-ups lost by each method setting, starting from the pilot")

 489def chart_allocation(bins, leader, runners, marks):
 490    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.8, 4.0))
 491    # A window with no such pulls has share 0, which a log axis can't show: it is left as a gap.
 492    series = [("others", BLUE, "All arms except {}".format(leader))]
 493    series += [("arm{}".format(arm), color, "Arm {}".format(arm)) for arm, color in zip(runners, (ORANGE, AQUA))]
 494    for column, color, name in series:
 495        ax.plot(bins["mid"], bins[column].where(bins[column] > 0), color=color, lw=2, marker="o", markersize=4,
 496                markeredgecolor=SURFACE, markeredgewidth=1, label=name)
 497    ax.set_xscale("log")
 498    ax.set_yscale("log")
 499    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(compact))
 500    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: "{:g}%".format(round(100 * v, 4))))
 501    top = ax.get_ylim()[1]
 502    for x, text in marks:
 503        ax.axvline(x, color=AXIS, lw=1, zorder=1)
 504        near_right = x > bins["hi"].iloc[-1] / 4  # Put the label left of a line close to the right edge
 505        ax.text(x / 1.06 if near_right else x * 1.06, top, text, fontsize=8, color=MUTED, va="top",
 506                ha="right" if near_right else "left")
 507    ax.set_xlabel("Pull number (log scale)")
 508    ax.set_ylabel("Share of pulls in the window")
 509    ax.legend(loc="lower left", fontsize=9)
 510    return to_svg(fig, "Share of pulls not on the leading arm, over the run")
 511

 513def chart_conversion(conv, leader, leader_rate):
 514    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.8, 4.0))
 515    pilot, after = conv.iloc[0], conv.iloc[1:]
 516    ax.plot(after["mid"], after["window"], color=GRAY, lw=1.5, marker="o", markersize=4.5,
 517            markeredgecolor=SURFACE, markeredgewidth=1, label="Each window")
 518    ax.scatter(pilot["hi"] / 2, pilot["window"], s=40, color=GRAY, edgecolors=SURFACE, linewidths=1.5, zorder=3)
 519    ax.annotate("Pilot", (pilot["hi"] / 2, pilot["window"]), xytext=(-8, 0), textcoords="offset points",
 520                fontsize=8.5, color=INK2, ha="right", va="center")
 521    ax.set_xlim(left=pilot["hi"] / 6)
 522    ax.plot(conv["hi"], conv["cumulative"], color=BLUE, lw=2, label="Cumulative, all pulls up to that point")
 523    ax.axhline(leader_rate, color=AXIS, lw=1, zorder=1)
 524    ax.text(pilot["hi"] / 2, leader_rate + 0.0012, "Arm {}'s overall rate, {}".format(leader, pct(leader_rate)),
 525            fontsize=8.5, color=INK2)
 526    ax.set_xscale("log")
 527    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(compact))
 528    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1, decimals=0))
 529    ax.set_xlabel("Pull number (log scale)")
 530    ax.set_ylabel("Conversion rate")
 531    ax.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=9)
 532    return to_svg(fig, "Cumulative and windowed conversion rate over the run")

 535def chart_stability(blocks, overall):
 536    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.8, 3.6))
 537    x = (blocks["first"] + blocks["last"]) / 2 / 1000
 538    ax.axhline(overall, color=AXIS, lw=1, zorder=1)
 539    ax.vlines(x, blocks["low"], blocks["high"], color=BLUE, lw=2, zorder=2)
 540    ax.scatter(x, blocks["rate"], s=40, color=BLUE, edgecolors=SURFACE, linewidths=1.5, zorder=3)
 541    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(1, decimals=2))
 542    ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(FuncFormatter(lambda v, _: compact(v * 1000) if v else "0"))
 543    ax.set_xlabel("Pull number (middle of each window)")
 544    ax.set_ylabel("Conversion rate")
 545    return to_svg(fig, "Leading arm's conversion rate in 20 windows of the run")

 567def table(headers, rows, align, classes=None):
 568    """align: one letter per column, l or r; an upper-case letter also stops the cells wrapping."""
 569    def cls(a):
 570        return " ".join(c for c, on in (("r", a in "rR"), ("nowrap", a.isupper())) if on)
 571
 572    head = "".join('<th class="{}">{}</th>'.format(cls(a), h) for h, a in zip(headers, align))
 573    body = []
 574    for i, row in enumerate(rows):
 575        row_cls = (classes or {}).get(i, "")
 576        cells = "".join('<td class="{}">{}</td>'.format(cls(a), c) for c, a in zip(row, align))
 577        body.append('<tr class="{}">{}</tr>'.format(row_cls, cells))
 578    return '<div class="scroll"><table><thead><tr>{}</tr></thead><tbody>{}</tbody></table></div>'.format(
 579        head, "".join(body))

 605def header(ctx):

 608    r = arms.loc[leader]
 609    tiles = [("Pulls used", "{:,}".format(n), "of {:,} ({})".format(MAX_PULLS, pct(n / MAX_PULLS, 1))),
 610             ("Total sign-ups", "{:,}".format(signups), "from {:,} visitors".format(V * n)),
 611             ("Conversion rate" if final else "Conversion so far", pct(signups / (V * n)), "pilot alone: {}".format(
 612                 pct(df["reward"].iloc[:PILOT_PULLS].sum() / (V * PILOT_PULLS)))),
 613             ("Chosen arm" if final else "Leading arm", "Arm {}".format(leader), "{} (95% interval {} to {})".format(
 614                 pct(r["rate"], 3), pct(r["low"], 3), pct(r["high"], 3)))]
 615    tile_html = "".join('<div class="tile"><div class="label">{}</div><div class="value">{}</div>'
 616                        '<div class="sub">{}</div></div>'.format(*map(esc, t)) for t in tiles)
 617    continuous = ctx["continuous_start"]
 618    steps =[("step0", "Step 0", "Screen methods on invented worlds", "Offline · 0 pulls"),
 619             ("step1", "Step 1", "Live pilot, 10 pulls per arm", "Live · 240 pulls"),
 620             ("step2", "Step 2", "Simulate the rest from the pilot", "Offline · 0 pulls"),
 621             ("step3", "Step 3", "Staged UCB ×0.05 with checkpoints", "Live · {:,} pulls".format(continuous - PILOT_PULLS)),
 622             ("step4", "Step 4", "Continuous run with tuning checks",
 623              "Live · {:,} pulls{}".format(n - continuous, "" if final else " so far")),
 624             ("results", "Results", "Live output" + ("" if final else " so far"), "")]
 625    flow = "".join('<a class="stepcard" href="#{}"><span class="no">{}</span><span class="t">{}</span>'
 626                   '<span class="p">{}</span></a>'.format(a, s, esc(t), esc(p)) for a, s, t, p in steps)
 627    return """
 628<header>
 629  <h1>Determining the best combination: code and analysis</h1>
 630  <div class="team"><div class="team-name">{team}</div>{members}</div>
 631  <div class="tiles">{tiles}</div>
 632  <p>This file walks through our experiment in the order we spent the pull budget. For each step we explain what
 633  we did and why, show the code we ran (with file names and line numbers from our repository), and then show the
 634  output. Steps 0 and 2 ran on our own computers and used no pulls; Steps 1, 3 and 4 used the live server.</p>
 635  <div class="flow">{flow}</div>
 636  <nav class="toc"><span class="lbl">Contents</span><ol>
 637    <li><a href="#overview">The problem and our approach</a></li>
 638    <li><a href="#step0">Step 0: screen methods on invented worlds</a></li>
 639    <li><a href="#step1">Step 1: live pilot</a></li>
 640    <li><a href="#step2">Step 2: simulate the rest of the budget from the pilot</a></li>
 641    <li><a href="#step3">Step 3: staged live run with UCB ×0.05</a></li>
 642    <li><a href="#step4">Step 4: continuous run with tuning checks</a></li>
 643    <li><a href="#results">Results{so_far}</a></li>
 644    <li><a href="#prompts">Appendix A: LLM use and prompts</a></li>
 645    <li><a href="#source">Appendix B: full source files</a></li>
 646  </ol></nav>
 647</header>""".format(team=esc(TEAM), members='<table class="members"><thead><tr><th>Name</th><th>Student Number</th>'
 648                    '</tr></thead><tbody>{}</tbody></table>'.format("".join(
 649                        "<tr><td>{}</td><td>{}</td></tr>".format(esc(name), esc(number)) for name, number in MEMBERS)),
 650                    tiles=tile_html, flow=flow, so_far="" if final else " so far")

 653def overview(ctx):
 654    runs = ctx["runs"]
 655    rows = []
 656    for i, run in enumerate(runs, 1):
 657        start, end = run["start"], run["end"]
 658        began = datetime.fromisoformat(start["timestamp"])
 659        before = start.get("history_pulls", 0)
 660        if end is None:
 661            after, outcome = len(ctx["df"]), "Still running when we exported this file"
 662        else:
 663            after = end.get("history_pulls", before + end.get("completed_pulls", 0))
 664            if end["event"] == "run_finished":
 665                outcome = {"budget_complete": "Completed its pull limit",
 666                           "group_budget_exhausted": "Used the rest of the 1,000,000-pull budget"}.get(
 667                    end.get("stop_reason"), end.get("stop_reason"))
 668            else:
 669                outcome = "We stopped it (Ctrl-C) with one request pending" if end.get(
 670                    "error_type") == "KeyboardInterrupt" else "Stopped: " + str(end.get("error_type"))
 671        method = "Uniform" if start["model"] == "uniform" else "UCB ×{:g}".format(
 672            round(multiplier(start["parameters"]["exploration"]), 6))
 673        budget = "All remaining" if start.get("budget") is None else "{:,}".format(start["budget"])
 674        rows.append([str(i), esc(when(began)), "{:,} → {:,}".format(before, after), esc(budget), esc(method),
 675                     esc(outcome)])
 676    runs_table = table(["Run", "Started (SGT)", "Saved pulls before → after", "Pull limit", "Method", "Outcome"],
 677                       rows, "lllrll") if rows else "<p>Our run list is not available in this export.</p>"
 678    body = """
 679<p>A website can combine 4 call-to-action buttons with 6 media options, giving 24 arms numbered 0 to 23. Each
 680pull shows one arm to 100 visitors and returns how many of them sign up. Our group had 1,000,000 pulls
 681(100 million visitors) and our goal was to maximise total sign-ups, so every pull spent on a weaker arm cost us
 682sign-ups. The budget, the server's pull counter and the limit of five requests per second are shared by the whole
 683group, so we agreed that one person would run a single driver for every live pull.</p>
 684<p><strong>Our approach in short:</strong> we compared methods on invented data before spending any pulls, took a
 685small live pilot, chose the method and its setting by simulating the rest of the budget from the pilot, and then
 686ran that method on the live server, stopping at fixed checkpoints to check the data before committing more of
 687the budget. During the long final run, the driver rechecked its setting every 200,000 pulls.</p>
 688<p>To make sure no pull was lost or counted twice, our driver saves every request (its arm, pull counter and
 689request ID) to a local SQLite database <em>before</em> sending it. If a response is lost, the driver retries the
 690same request with the same ID, following the handout's recovery steps, and it saves each response in the same
 691transaction that clears the pending request. Our event log records every live run:</p>
 692{runs}
 693""".format(runs=runs_table)
 694    return section("overview", "The problem and our approach", "", body)

 697def step0(ctx):
 698    path = STEP0_DIR / "results" / "mean_regret.csv"
 699    if not path.is_file():
 700        return section("step0", "Step 0: screen methods on invented worlds", "Offline · 0 pulls",
 701                       "<p>Our Step 0 results are not available in this export.</p>")
 702    data = pd.read_csv(path)
 703    worlds = [("wide", "Wide spread"), ("factorial", "Button × media"), ("clear_winner", "One clear winner"),
 704              ("close_race", "Close race"), ("extra_noise", "Extra noise"), ("rates_change", "Rates change")]
 705    best = {w: data[w].min() for w, _ in worlds}
 706    rows = []
 707    for r in data.itertuples(index=False):
 708        cells = [esc(r.label.replace("e-greedy", "ε-greedy").replace(" e=", " ε=").replace("Fixed ", "")
 709                     .replace(" x0.", " ×0."))]
 710        for w, _ in worlds:
 711            v = getattr(r, w)
 712            cells.append(("<strong>{:,.0f}</strong>" if v == best[w] else "{:,.0f}").format(v / 1000))
 713        rows.append(cells)
 714    sim = "../offline_simulation/simulate.py"
 715    body = """
 716<p>Before making any live pull, we built a simulator with <em>invented</em> conversion rates to see how different
 717methods behave. It never contacts the server. We tested the three methods from our original plan (explore-first,
 718ε-greedy and UCB1), adaptive ε-greedy from Lecture 9, and Thompson Sampling. We ran each setting 100 times in each
 719of six kinds of world over the full 1,000,000 pulls, starting from 100 pulls per arm. Because the rates are
 720invented, we used this step only to decide which methods to carry forward.</p>
 721{label_code}
 722{c1}{c2}{c3}
 723{label_out}
 724<p class="cap">Simulated sign-ups lost against always pulling the true best arm, in thousands (mean of 100 runs).
 725Bold marks the lowest in each world.</p>
 726{table}
 727{label_take}
 728{take}
 729""".format(label_code=label("Code"),
 730           c1=code(excerpt(sim, "_factorial"), "how a button × media world is made"),
 731           c2=code(excerpt(sim, "SCENARIOS"), "our six worlds (we used gap7 and gap2 only for pilot-size tests)"),
 732           c3=code(excerpt(sim, "run_loop"), "one pull at a time for UCB, Thompson Sampling and ε-greedy", open_=False),
 733           label_out=label("Output (simulated)"),
 734           table=table(["Method"] + [esc(t) for _, t in worlds], rows, "l" + "r" * len(worlds)),
 735           label_take=label("What we learned"),
 736           take=bullets([
 737               "Thompson Sampling and UCB with a scaled-down bonus (×0.02 to ×0.05) lost the fewest sign-ups in "
 738               "every fixed-rate world, about 7,000 to 20,000.",
 739               "UCB1 with the lecture's bonus (×1) lost 0.9 to 1.2 million. Its bonus is sized for rewards as noisy "
 740               "as a single 0-or-1 outcome, but the conversion rate of a 100-visitor batch is far less noisy, so it "
 741               "kept exploring.",
 742               "Explore-first and ε-greedy depended heavily on their setting, and explore-first could not recover "
 743               "from an early wrong pick.",
 744               "When the rates changed part-way through, every method lost heavily, so we planned noise and "
 745               "stability checks at each live checkpoint.",
 746               "A bigger pilot only cost sign-ups when the method kept learning afterwards, so we cut our live pilot "
 747               "from the planned 100 pulls per arm to 10."]))
 748    return section("step0", "Step 0: screen methods on invented worlds", "Offline · 0 pulls", body)

 751def step1(ctx):
 752    df, pilot, leader = ctx["df"], ctx["pilot"], ctx["leader"]
 753    noise_ratio = use_function("phase1/main.py", "noise_ratio", mean=mean, variance=variance, VISITORS_PER_PULL=V)
 754    stability = use_function("phase1/main.py", "stability", mean=mean, math=math, VISITORS_PER_PULL=V)
 755    by_arm = [df["reward"].iloc[:PILOT_PULLS][df["arm"].iloc[:PILOT_PULLS] == a].tolist() for a in range(K)]
 756    ratio, dof = noise_ratio(by_arm)
 757    scores, overall = stability(by_arm)
 758    first = df.iloc[0]
 759    ctx["pilot_checks"] = (ratio, dof, scores, overall)
 760    rows, classes = [], {}
 761    for i, (arm, r) in enumerate(pilot.sort_values("rate", ascending=False).iterrows()):
 762        rows.append([str(arm), "{:,}".format(int(r["pulls"])), "{:,}".format(int(r["signups"])), pct(r["rate"], 1),
 763                     "{} to {}".format(pct(r["low"], 1), pct(r["high"], 1)), p_label(r["p_best"])])
 764        if arm == leader:
 765            classes[i] = "hl"
 766    checks = ("Test pull: pull {pull} on arm {arm} returned {reward} sign-ups (NetReward {net}), saved {t} SGT.\n"
 767              "Pilot: {n} pulls, {s:,} sign-ups ({rate}).\n"
 768              "Noise: batch variance is {ratio:.2f} times binomial (about 1 ± {tol:.2f} is normal).\n"
 769              "Stability: {moved} of {arms} arms moved by more than 2 standard errors between their first and last "
 770              "5 pulls (0 to 3 is normal).\nAll arms together moved {overall:+.1f} standard errors.").format(
 771        pull=int(first["pull"]), arm=int(first["arm"]), reward=int(first["reward"]), net=int(first["net_reward"]),
 772        t=when(first["time"]), n=PILOT_PULLS, s=int(df["reward"].iloc[:PILOT_PULLS].sum()),
 773        rate=pct(df["reward"].iloc[:PILOT_PULLS].sum() / (V * PILOT_PULLS)), ratio=ratio, tol=2 * math.sqrt(2 / dof),
 774        moved=sum(abs(s) > 2 for s in scores), arms=len(scores), overall=overall)
 775    contenders = pilot[(pilot["p_best"] >= 0.005) & (pilot.index != leader)].sort_values("rate", ascending=False)
 776    r = pilot.loc[leader]
 777    body = """
 778<p>We pulled every arm 10 times in rotation: 240 pulls, or 0.024% of the budget. We made a single test pull first
 779to confirm that live pulls worked and returned the expected fields, and made the other 239 once it checked out.
 780Our uniform model always pulls the least-pulled arm (the lowest number on ties), so the pilot sampled every arm
 781evenly over time. We chose 10 pulls per arm rather than the 100 in our original plan because Step 0 showed that
 782a bigger pilot costs sign-ups without helping a method that keeps learning. Ten pulls still gave each arm 1,000
 783visitors.</p>
 784<p>We then checked the two assumptions our next step relies on: is the batch-to-batch noise binomial, and did any
 785arm drift between its first and last pulls?</p>
 786{lc}{c1}{c2}{c3}{c4}{c5}
 787{lo}{out}
 788{fig}
 789{tab}
 790{an}
 791{lt}
 792{take}
 793""".format(
 794        lc=label("Code"),
 795        c1=code(excerpt("phase1/config.py"), "our pilot settings (the password is typed in at run time, never stored)"),
 796        c2=code(excerpt("program/bandit/models.py", "UniformModel.select_arm"), "which arm the pilot pulls next"),
 797        c3=code(excerpt("program/bandit/storage.py", "HistoryStore.prepare"),
 798                "a request is saved before it is sent", open_=False),
 799        c4=code(excerpt("program/bandit/storage.py", "HistoryStore.complete"),
 800                "the response is checked against the pending request and saved", open_=False),
 801        c5=code(excerpt("phase1/main.py", "noise_ratio")) + code(excerpt("phase1/main.py", "stability")),
 802        lo=label("Output (live)"), out=output(checks),
 803        fig=figure(chart_pilot(pilot, leader), "Pilot results by arm",
 804                   "Beta(1 + sign-ups, 1 + non-sign-ups) posterior after 10 pulls per arm. "
 805                   "P(best) is the share of 400,000 joint posterior draws in which the arm is highest."),
 806        tab='<details class="analysis"><summary>Table view: all 24 arms</summary>{}</details>'.format(
 807            table(["Arm", "Pulls", "Sign-ups", "Rate", "95% interval", "P(best)"], rows, "rrrrrr", classes)),
 808        an=analysis_code("arm_summary", "prob_best"),
 809        lt=label("What we learned"),
 810        take=bullets([
 811            "Arm {} led at {} (95% interval {} to {}), with a {} chance of being the best arm.".format(
 812                leader, pct(r["rate"], 1), pct(r["low"], 1), pct(r["high"], 1), p_label(r["p_best"])),
 813            "Arms {} ({} to {}) still had a small chance of being best, so our method needed to keep testing "
 814            "them.".format(", ".join(str(a) for a in contenders.index), pct(contenders["rate"].min(), 1),
 815                           pct(contenders["rate"].max(), 1))
 816            if len(contenders) else "No other arm had a material chance of being best.",
 817            "Noise was close to binomial and no arm drifted unusually, so in Step 2 we could model each arm with a "
 818            "Beta posterior and a fixed rate."]))
 819    return section("step1", "Step 1: live pilot", "Live · 240 pulls", body, live=True)

 822def step2(ctx):
 823    base = REPO / "phase2" / "results"
 824    summary = pd.read_csv(base / "summary.csv")
 825    validation = pd.read_csv(base / "validation.csv")
 826    runs = pd.read_csv(base / "runs.csv", usecols=["stage", "combination", "regret"])
 827    worst = runs.groupby(["stage", "combination"])["regret"].max()
 828    chosen = "UCB x0.05, 10/arm"
 829
 830    def name(combo):
 831        return (combo.replace("x", "×").replace("e-greedy", "ε-greedy").replace(", 10/arm", ", from the pilot")
 832                .replace("/arm", " per arm first"))
 833
 834    rows, classes = [], {}
 835    for i, r in enumerate(validation.itertuples()):
 836        behind = "Leader" if r.rank == 1 else "{:,.0f} ± {:,.0f}".format(r.vs_leader, 2 * r.vs_leader_se)
 837        rows.append([str(r.rank), esc(name(r.combination)), "{:,.0f} ± {:,.0f}".format(r.regret, 2 * r.regret_se),
 838                     behind, "{:,.0f}".format(worst[("validate", r.combination)]), pct(r.picks_best, 1),
 839                     pct(r.best_share, 1)])
 840        if r.combination == chosen:
 841            classes[i] = "hl"
 842    top_rows = []
 843    for combo, label_ in (("Thompson", "Thompson Sampling"), ("UCB x0.05", "UCB ×0.05"), ("UCB x0.02", "UCB ×0.02")):
 844        cells = [esc(label_)]
 845        for per_arm in (10, 25, 50, 100):
 846            hit = summary[summary["combination"] == "{}, {}/arm".format(combo, per_arm)]
 847            cells.append("{:,.0f}".format(hit["regret"].iloc[0]))
 848        top_rows.append(cells)
 849    p2 = validation.set_index("combination")
 850    ts, ucb = p2.loc["Thompson, 10/arm"], p2.loc[chosen]
 851    luck = math.sqrt(V * MAX_PULLS * 0.245 * 0.755)
 852    body = """
 853<p>We turned the pilot into plausible "worlds" and played every candidate out to 1,000,000 pulls in each. We gave
 854each arm a Beta(1 + sign-ups, 1 + non-sign-ups) distribution from its pilot result, and each world draws one true
 855rate per arm from these distributions. We used 200 worlds. Each combination is a number of uniform pulls per arm
 856(10, which is the pilot itself, or a top-up to 25, 50 or 100), followed by UCB (8 bonus multipliers), ε-greedy
 857(5 values of ε) or Thompson Sampling: 56 combinations in all. We ran every combination on the same worlds, so the
 858differences between them come from the method rather than from luck. We scored each one by the sign-ups it lost
 859against always pulling that world's true best arm. Because the best of 56 on the same worlds looks better than it
 860really is, we reran the top 5, plus each method's best, on 200 fresh worlds.</p>
 861{lc}{c0}{c1}{c2}{c3}
 862{lo}
 863{fig}
 864<p class="cap">Rerun on 200 fresh worlds (simulated). Sign-ups lost are against always pulling the true best arm,
 865which would earn about {oracle} in total. ± is 2 standard errors.</p>
 866{val}
 867<p class="cap">Extra uniform pulls before the method (simulated sign-ups lost, mean of 200 worlds):</p>
 868{top}
 869<div class="callout"><strong>Our decision: UCB ×0.05, starting straight from the pilot.</strong>
 870Thompson Sampling was best on the fresh worlds ({ts_r:,.0f} ± {ts_se:,.0f} lost) and UCB ×0.05 came second,
 871{gap:,.0f} ± {gap_se:,.0f} sign-ups behind. That gap is about 0.003% of the total, while luck alone moves the live
 872total by about ±{luck:,.0f} (one standard deviation), so the difference between the two would not have been
 873visible in our result. We chose UCB ×0.05 because:
 874{reasons}
 875</div>
 876{lt}
 877{take}
 878""".format(
 879        lc=label("Code"),
 880        c0=code(excerpt("phase2/config.py"), "the grid of combinations"),
 881        c1=code(excerpt("phase2/simulate.py", "posterior"), "the pilot becomes a Beta posterior for each arm"),
 882        c2=code(excerpt("phase2/simulate.py", "draw_worlds"), "one world = one true rate per arm"),
 883        c3=code(excerpt("phase2/simulate.py", "run_policy"), "UCB, ε-greedy and Thompson Sampling, one pull at a time",
 884                open_=False),
 885        lo=label("Output (simulated)"),
 886        fig=figure(chart_phase2(summary, worst.loc["compare"], chosen),
 887                   "Every setting, starting straight from the pilot",
 888                   "Simulated on 200 worlds drawn from the pilot. The dot is the mean loss; the line runs to the "
 889                   "worst world. Our choice is in bold."),
 890        oracle="{:,.1f} million".format((ts["total_signups"] + ts["regret"]) / 1e6),
 891        val=table(["Rank", "Combination", "Lost vs best arm", "Behind the leader", "Worst world", "Picks best arm",
 892                   "Pulls on best arm"], rows, "rlrrrrr", classes),
 893        top=table(["Method", "10 per arm (pilot only)", "25 per arm", "50 per arm", "100 per arm"], top_rows, "lrrrr"),
 894        ts_r=ts["regret"], ts_se=2 * ts["regret_se"], gap=ucb["vs_leader"], gap_se=2 * ucb["vs_leader_se"], luck=luck,
 895        reasons=bullets([
 896            "It is the model we had already built and tested in <code>program/bandit</code>, which our live driver "
 897            "uses. Switching to Thompson Sampling would have meant running new, untested code on a budget that "
 898            "cannot be redone.",
 899            "UCB has no randomness, so every choice can be replayed from our saved data and explained. We replay all "
 900            "of them in the Results section.",
 901            "Its worst world lost only {:,.0f}. UCB ×0.02 had a similar mean but lost {:,.0f} in its worst world.".format(
 902                worst[("validate", chosen)], worst[("validate", "UCB x0.02, 10/arm")]),
 903            "UCB is part of the course content; Thompson Sampling is not."]),
 904        lt=label("What we learned"),
 905        take=bullets([
 906            "We should start the method straight from the pilot: topping up to 100 pulls per arm cost about 21,000 "
 907            "more sign-ups, whichever method followed.",
 908            "The lecture's UCB1 bonus (×1) lost about 719,000 and the best ε-greedy setting about 104,000, far "
 909            "behind scaled UCB and Thompson Sampling.",
 910            "These figures are simulated. They assume binomial noise and fixed rates, which we had to confirm at the "
 911            "live checkpoints."]))
 912    return section("step2", "Step 2: simulate the rest of the budget from the pilot", "Offline · 0 pulls", body)

 915def step3(ctx):
 916    df, leader = ctx["df"], ctx["leader"]
 917    decisions = pd.read_csv(REPO / "phase3" / "results" / "decisions.csv")
 918    explore = decisions[decisions["kind"] == "explore"]
 919    sample = pd.concat([decisions.head(2), explore.head(4)])
 920    sample_rows = [[str(r.pull), str(r.arm), pct(r.mean), "{:.4f}".format(r.bonus), "{:.4f}".format(r.score),
 921                    "{} ({:.4f})".format(r.runner_up, r.runner_up_score), str(r.leader), esc(r.kind)]
 922                   for r in sample.itertuples()]
 923    cuts = [PILOT_PULLS, *CHECKPOINTS, ctx["continuous_start"]]
 924    view = checkpoint_view(df, cuts, leader)
 925    view_rows = [["{:,}".format(v["cut"]), "{} ({:,} pulls)".format(pct(v["leader_rate"]), v["leader_pulls"]),
 926                  "Arm {}: {} ({:,} pulls)".format(v["runner"], pct(v["runner_rate"]), v["runner_pulls"]),
 927                  p_label(v["p_best"])] for v in view]
 928    recovery_path = REPO / "phase3" / "results" / "pending_recovery_2026-11-12.json"
 929    recovery = ""
 930    if recovery_path.is_file():
 931        rec = json.loads(recovery_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 932        recovery = output(("Recovered pull {:,} on arm {}: Reward {}. Fresh requests created during recovery: {}.\n"
 933                           "Server and local history after recovery: {:,} pulls and {:,} sign-ups each, no pending "
 934                           "request.").format(rec["recovered_pull"], rec["arm"], rec["reward"],
 935                                              rec["fresh_requests_created"], rec["after_pulls"], rec["after_signups"]))
 936    body = """
 937<p>Our live method, UCB, gives each arm an optimistic score (its mean rate plus a bonus) and pulls the arm with
 938the highest score:</p>
 939<p class="formula">score = mean rate + 0.05 × √(2 ln t ÷ n)</p>
 940<p>Here t is the total number of pulls so far and n is that arm's pulls. The bonus shrinks as an arm is pulled,
 941so a rarely pulled arm gets another look only while its score can still beat the leader's. In our code this is
 942<code>UCBModel(exploration=0.005)</code>, because exploration = 2 × 0.05². Because we tuned the ×0.05 multiplier
 943by simulation, we treat the score as an optimistic score rather than a calibrated confidence bound.</p>
 944<p>We started straight from the pilot data and stopped at two checkpoints to review the results before spending
 945more: {c1:,} pulls on 10 November and {c2:,} on 11 November. We then made several shorter runs to measure and
 946improve the request speed. We stopped one of them by hand at pull 15,054 while a request was in flight; our next
 947run recovered that exact request (same arm, counter and request ID) before making any new choice. A final
 948,000-pull run timed the driver with tuning switched on.</p>
 949{lc}{c1x}{c2x}{c3x}{c4x}
 950{lo}
 951<p class="cap">What we saw at each checkpoint (live data up to that pull):</p>
 952{view}
 953<p class="cap">Stage 1 decision log: for every pull, our driver records the chosen arm's mean, bonus and score,
 954and the runner-up. Shown here are the first two pulls and the first four exploring pulls.</p>
 955{sample}
 956{dec}
 957{rec}
 958{lt}
 959{take}
 960""".format(
 961        c1=CHECKPOINTS[0], c2=CHECKPOINTS[1], lc=label("Code"),
 962        c1x=code(excerpt("program/bandit/models.py", "UCBModel"), "the score and the choice"),
 963        c2x=code(excerpt("phase3/main.py", "exploration"), "multiplier 0.05 → exploration 0.005"),
 964        c3x=code(excerpt("phase3/config.py"), "phase 3 settings", open_=False),
 965        c4x=code(excerpt("program/bandit/runner.py", "_resolve"),
 966                 "an uncertain request is retried with the same identity until it resolves", open_=False),
 967        lo=label("Output (live)"),
 968        view=table(["At pull", "Arm {} rate".format(leader), "Runner-up", "P(arm {} is best)".format(leader)],
 969                   view_rows, "rrrr"),
 970        sample=table(["Pull", "Arm", "Mean", "Bonus", "Score", "Runner-up (score)", "Leader", "Kind"],
 971                     sample_rows, "rrrrrrrl"),
 972        dec=output(("Stage 1: {:,} pulls. Exploit (the arm with the highest mean was pulled): {:,}. Explore: {:,} ({}).\n"
 973                    "Every saved choice replays exactly: {}.\nExpected cost of exploring, judged by the means at the "
 974                    "time: {:,.0f} sign-ups.").format(
 975            len(decisions), int((decisions["kind"] == "exploit").sum()), len(explore), pct(len(explore) / len(decisions), 0),
 976            "yes" if decisions["replay_matches"].all() else "no", 100 * explore["mean_gap_to_leader"].sum())),
 977        rec=recovery,
 978        lt=label("What we learned"),
 979        take=bullets([
 980            "At 1,200 pulls arm {} still led, but its rate had fallen from the pilot's {} towards 24.5%, and arm {} "
 981            "had risen. UCB spent extra pulls on the runner-up exactly where the question was still open.".format(
 982                leader, pct(view[0]["leader_rate"], 1), view[1]["runner"]),
 983            "By 5,000 pulls arm {}'s chance of being best was {}, and our noise and stability checks were still "
 984            "normal, so we let the method run continuously.".format(leader, p_label(view[2]["p_best"])),
 985            "Our recovery process worked as designed on a real interruption: the one pending request was resolved "
 986            "once, and the server and local totals agreed afterwards."]))
 987    return section("step3", "Step 3: staged live run with UCB ×0.05", "Live · {:,} pulls".format(
 988        ctx["continuous_start"] - PILOT_PULLS), body, live=True)

 991def checks_text(numbers):
 992    """[1, 2, 3, 4] -> "Checks 1 to 4"; [2] -> "Check 2"; [1, 3] -> "Checks 1 and 3"."""
 993    if len(numbers) == 1:
 994        return "Check {}".format(numbers[0])
 995    if numbers == list(range(numbers[0], numbers[-1] + 1)):
 996        return "Checks {} to {}".format(numbers[0], numbers[-1])
 997    return "Checks {} and {}".format(", ".join(map(str, numbers[:-1])), numbers[-1])
 998

1000def switch_detail(df, tuning, number, leader, continuous_start):
1001    """What a tuning switch was based on, and what the pulls after it did."""
1002    d = tuning[number - 1]
1003    cut = d["at_pull"]
1004    g = arm_summary(df.iloc[:cut], draws=20_000)
1005    se = np.sqrt(g["rate"] * (1 - g["rate"]) / (V * g["pulls"]))
1006    z = ((g["rate"][leader] - g["rate"]) / np.sqrt(se ** 2 + se[leader] ** 2)).drop(index=leader)
1007    base = next(c for c in d["candidates"] if c["multiplier"] == d["baseline_multiplier"])
1008    end = tuning[number]["at_pull"] if number < len(tuning) else len(df)
1009    previous_start = tuning[number - 2]["at_pull"] if number >= 2 else continuous_start
1010    return {"runner": int(z.idxmin()), "z": float(z.min()), "left": d["horizon"], "base_loss": base["expected_full_regret"],
1011            "loss_cut": -d["validation"]["full_regret_difference"], "cvar_cut": -d["validation"]["cvar_difference"],
1012            "after": end - cut, "after_on_leader": float((df["arm"].iloc[cut:end] == leader).mean()),
1013            "previous": cut - previous_start, "previous_off": int((df["arm"].iloc[previous_start:cut] != leader).sum())}
1014
1015
1016def step4(ctx):
1017    df, tuning, final, leader = ctx["df"], ctx["tuning"], ctx["final"], ctx["leader"]
1018    multipliers = sorted({c["multiplier"] for d in tuning for c in d["candidates"]})
1019    headers = ["Multiplier"] + ["Check {}<br>pull {:,}".format(i + 1, d["at_pull"]) for i, d in enumerate(tuning)]
1020    rows = []
1021    for m in multipliers:
1022        cells = ["×{:g}".format(m)]
1023        for d in tuning:
1024            c = next(c for c in d["candidates"] if c["multiplier"] == m)
1025            text = "{:,.0f} ± {:,.0f}<br>CVaR {:,.0f}".format(c["expected_full_regret"], 2 * c["full_regret_mc_se"],
1026                                                             c["cvar"])
1027            cells.append("<strong>{}</strong>".format(text) if m == d["baseline_multiplier"] else text)
1028        rows.append(cells)
1029    rows.append(["Decision"] + ["Kept ×{:g}".format(d["selected_multiplier"])
1030                                if d["selected_multiplier"] == d["baseline_multiplier"]
1031                                else "Switched to ×{:g}".format(d["selected_multiplier"]) for d in tuning])
1032    kept = [i + 1 for i, d in enumerate(tuning) if d["selected_multiplier"] == d["baseline_multiplier"]]
1033    switched = [i + 1 for i, d in enumerate(tuning) if d["selected_multiplier"] != d["baseline_multiplier"]]
1034    outcome = []
1035    if kept:
1036        outcome.append("{} kept ×{:g}.".format(checks_text(kept), tuning[kept[0] - 1]["baseline_multiplier"]))
1037    for no in switched:
1038        d = tuning[no - 1]
1039        outcome.append("Check {} at pull {:,}, with {:,} pulls left, switched to ×{:g}{}.".format(
1040            no, d["at_pull"], d["horizon"], d["selected_multiplier"], " for the rest of the run" if no == len(tuning) else ""))
1041    if not final and ctx["tuning_state_next"]:
1042        outcome.append("The next check is due at pull {:,}.".format(ctx["tuning_state_next"]))
1043    first = next(c for c in tuning[0]["candidates"] if c["multiplier"] == tuning[0]["baseline_multiplier"])
1044    last = next(c for c in tuning[-1]["candidates"] if c["multiplier"] == tuning[-1]["baseline_multiplier"])
1045    take = [
1046        "Our simulated expected loss over the remaining budget fell from about {:,.0f} sign-ups at check 1 to about "
1047        "{:,.0f} at check {}, as our data separated arm {} more clearly from the others at every stage.".format(
1048            first["expected_full_regret"], last["expected_full_regret"], len(tuning), leader),
1049        "At check 1, ×0.03 had a slightly lower expected loss than ×0.05 but a higher CVaR, so our safeguard kept "
1050        "×0.05. Larger multipliers (×0.075 and ×0.10) would have explored more and lost more at every check."]
1051    for no in switched:
1052        s, d = switch_detail(df, tuning, no, leader, ctx["continuous_start"]), tuning[no - 1]
1053        take.append(
1054            "At check {no}, arm {leader} was {z:.1f} standard errors ahead of arm {runner} and only {left:,} pulls were "
1055            "left. Under the current model and remaining budget, simulations favoured reducing exploration to ×{n:g}. ×{b:g} would still have spent a few pulls on "
1056            "the runners-up (about {bl:,.0f} sign-ups lost in expectation), whereas ×{n:g} made their bonus too small "
1057            "to overtake arm {leader}. On fresh simulated worlds, ×{n:g} lowered the expected loss by {lc:.1f} sign-ups "
1058            "and CVaR by {cc:,.0f}, so the switch passed every safeguard.".format(
1059                no=no, leader=leader, z=s["z"], runner=s["runner"], left=s["left"], b=d["baseline_multiplier"],
1060                bl=s["base_loss"], n=d["selected_multiplier"], lc=s["loss_cut"], cc=s["cvar_cut"]))
1061        take.append(
1062            "{} of the {:,} pulls after check {} went to arm {}. The stage before it had put {} of its {:,} pulls "
1063            "elsewhere. Independent validation estimated an expected gain of {gain:.1f} sign-ups from the switch.".format(
1064                "All" if s["after_on_leader"] == 1 else pct(s["after_on_leader"], 3), s["after"], no, leader,
1065                s["previous_off"], s["previous"], gain=s["loss_cut"]))
1066    take.append("The tuning checks are simulations based on our live data. We used them to support the choice of "
1067                "setting; they are not live results.")
1068    body = """
1069<p>From pull {start:,}, a single driver ran continuously until the budget was used, sending one request at a time
1070with at least 0.25 seconds between requests. It printed progress every 1,000 pulls, and a first Ctrl-C would have
1071stopped it only after the in-flight response was saved.</p>
1072<p>Every 200,000 pulls, the driver paused for one to two minutes to recheck the multiplier. It simulated the whole
1073remaining budget from the current posteriors, trying candidates from ×0.02 to ×0.10 for the next stage. We set it
1074to switch only if a candidate was clearly better on expected loss over the remaining budget, no worse on
1075next-stage loss and no worse on the average loss in the worst 5% of simulated worlds (CVaR 95%), and only if the
1076improvement held up on a fresh set of simulated worlds. Otherwise it kept the current setting.</p>
1077<p>{outcome}</p>
1078{lc}{c1}{c2}
1079{lo}
1080<p class="cap">Simulated expected sign-ups lost over the remaining budget at each check (± 2 Monte Carlo standard
1081errors), and CVaR 95%: the mean loss in the worst 5% of worlds. Lower is better. Bold marks the multiplier in use
1082when the check ran.</p>
1083{table}
1084{lt}
1085{take}
1086""".format(
1087        start=ctx["continuous_start"], outcome=" ".join(outcome), lc=label("Code"),
1088        c1=code(excerpt("program/bandit/tuning.py", "evaluate"), "rank the candidates on simulated worlds", open_=False),
1089        c2=code(excerpt("program/bandit/tuning.py", "validate_switch"),
1090                "a switch must pass every safeguard on fresh worlds", open_=False),
1091        lo=label("Output (simulated from live data)"),
1092        table=table(headers, rows, "l" + "R" * len(tuning), {len(rows) - 1: "total"}),
1093        lt=label("What we learned"), take=bullets(take))
1094    return section("step4", "Step 4: continuous run with tuning checks", "Live · {}".format(
1095        "complete" if final else "in progress"), body, live=True)
1096
